title: Dogfooding round 1 hardening
body: Six small gaps surfaced by dogfooding `asf` (Rust workspace that dispatches Claude Code workers into git worktrees). (1) `gh sync` must ignore remote issues authored by someone other than the authenticated GitHub user and report them in a `foreign` field; (2) `asf doctor` gets a `github` check that depends on `[merge] target`; (3) a new `asf lane clean <id> [--dry-run]` removes a finished worktree without `--force`, keeping the branch; `worktree_remove` also accepts rebase-merged branches via `git cherry`; (4) gates whose output contains `LNK1104` are retried up to 3 attempts with a 3 s pause, reported via `GateResult.attempts`; (5) `asf plan new` renders a `Language:` line from `[methodology] language` into both planner prompts; (6) `asf plan new` takes its prompt stages and schemas from the active methodology (embedded builtins or local manifests) instead of four `include_str!` constants. Shared struct changes (`GhIssue.author`, `GateResult.attempts`, both `#[serde(default)]`) land first in one foundation task so the parallel tracks stay file-disjoint. Out of scope: Vcs trait, ports.rs, Cargo manifests, spec-kit/superpowers manifests, new CLI commands beyond `lane clean`, TUI, retries on anything but LNK1104.

title: Add GhIssue.author and GateResult.attempts fields (serde default) and fix all construction sites
body: Foundation task; no behaviour change. (a) Add `#[serde(default)] pub author: <type>` to `GhIssue` in `crates/asf-core/src/github.rs` (line ~60). Use `String` defaulting to empty (an empty author never equals `whoami`, so unknown authors are treated as foreign; fail-closed). Match the existing style of neighbouring string fields. (b) Add `#[serde(default)] pub attempts: u32` to `GateResult` in `crates/asf-core/src/vcs.rs` (line ~72). Default 0 means 'not run / unknown' for deserialised legacy records; runners set it to the real attempt count. (c) Fix EVERY struct-literal site in one pass before compiling: `crates/asf-core/src/run.rs:205`, `crates/asf-vcs/src/gates.rs:43` and `:104` (set `attempts: 1` in run_gate's paths, no retry logic yet), `crates/asf-vcs/src/gh.rs:123`, `crates/asf-vcs/src/fake_github.rs:231`, `crates/asf-store/tests/runs.rs:155`. Verify with Grep for `GhIssue {` and `GateResult {` across `crates/` before running cargo. Do NOT implement author fetching (task 2) or retry (task 5).

acceptance.text: `cargo build --workspace` succeeds with no remaining `GhIssue {` or `GateResult {` literal missing the new field (grep verified).
`cargo test --workspace` passes unchanged (no new behaviour asserted).
A JSON record without `author` / `attempts` deserialises with the default value (unit test next to the type, TDD RED then GREEN).
`cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass.

title: gh sync: whoami and foreign-issue filter
body: Implement `GitHub::whoami(&self) -> Result<String, _>` on the GitHub port (trait in `crates/asf-core/src/github.rs`). Fake (`crates/asf-vcs/src/fake_github.rs`) returns `me`. Real impl in `crates/asf-vcs/src/gh.rs` runs `gh api user --jq .login`. Extend `issue_list` in `gh.rs` to request `author` in `gh issue list --json ...,author` and fill `GhIssue.author` (field added in task 1). In the `gh sync` command (locate via Grep for `foreign`/`mirror` under `crates/asf/src/commands/`), a remote issue whose author differs from `whoami()` is never used as a mirror and is listed in the new output field `foreign: [{id, number, author}]`. If `whoami()` fails, abort with a backend error (exit 1); do not treat every issue as foreign. Do not change mirror or uid semantics beyond this filter. Write tests first (RED). Use thiserror in libraries, anyhow only in the binary. Emit the `--json` envelope.

acceptance.text: `cargo test -p asf-vcs --test github` passes, including a case where a foreign-authored remote issue is excluded from mirroring and appears in `foreign`.
`cargo test -p asf --test cli_github` passes; output JSON contains `foreign` with `id`, `number`, `author`.
When fake `whoami` errors, `gh sync` exits 1 with a backend error and mirrors nothing.
Gates from the brief pass for the whole workspace.

title: Doctor github check driven by [merge] target
body: Add a `github` check to `asf doctor`. When `[merge] target = "github"`, the check is required: it runs `gh auth status` (ok on exit 0, fail otherwise) and `git remote get-url <remote>` (ok when it resolves). When target is `local`, the check is `warn`/skipped and never fails the command. Locate the existing doctor implementation via Grep for `doctor` under `crates/asf/src/commands/` and follow its check/result pattern. Do not add new CLI commands. Write tests first (RED), covering: github target with ok gh, github target with failing `gh auth status`, local target.

acceptance.text: `cargo test -p asf --test cli_repo` covers github target success, github target with failing `gh auth status` (check fails, exit 1), and local target (warn/skipped, command does not fail).
JSON output includes the github check with a detail string taken from `gh auth status` / `git remote get-url`.
Gates from the brief pass for the whole workspace.

title: worktree_remove: accept rebase-merged branches via git cherry; refuse empty branches on that path
body: Extend `Vcs::worktree_remove` implementation in `crates/asf-vcs/src/git.rs` (line ~91; it is also called from `worker.rs:283`, keep its signature and behaviour for that caller). A branch counts as merged when the existing ancestor check passes OR when `git cherry <base> <branch>` prints no `+` lines AND `git rev-list --count <base>..<branch>` > 0 (resolved open question 2: a fresh lane with zero commits ahead must NOT count as merged). Keep the ancestor path unchanged. Do NOT modify the `Vcs` trait or `crates/asf-core/src/ports.rs`. Do not delete branches. Write tests first in `crates/asf-vcs/tests/git.rs`: rebase-merged branch is removable; branch with unique commits is refused; branch with zero commits ahead is refused.

acceptance.text: `cargo test -p asf-vcs --test git` passes with the three cases above (rebase-merged removable, unique commits refused, zero commits ahead refused).
Existing worker cleanup tests (`cargo test --workspace`) still pass.
Gates from the brief pass for the whole workspace.

title: asf lane clean <id> [--dry-run]
body: Add `Clean { id, dry_run }` to `LaneCmd` in `crates/asf/src/cli.rs` (line ~395) and implement it in `crates/asf/src/commands/lane.rs`. Behaviour: refuse with conflict (exit 3) while the issue is claimed or the worktree is dirty; otherwise call `worktree_remove` on `<worktrees_dir>/<id>` WITHOUT force, keep the branch, return `{id, worktree, removed}` in the `--json` envelope. `--dry-run` returns `removed: false` and changes nothing. No `--force`, no branch deletion, no removal of claimed lanes. Use task 4's merged-detection via `worktree_remove`. Write tests first in `crates/asf/tests/cli_lane.rs`.

acceptance.text: `cargo test -p asf --test cli_lane` covers: clean of finished lane removes the worktree and keeps the branch; claimed lane refused with exit 3; dirty worktree refused with exit 3; `--dry-run` reports `removed: false` and leaves the worktree in place.
`asf lane --help` lists `clean` with `--dry-run`; no `--force` flag exists.
Gates from the brief pass for the whole workspace.

title: Retry gates on LNK1104 (3 attempts, 3 s pause)
body: In `crates/asf-vcs/src/gates.rs`: when a gate's output contains `LNK1104`, rerun it after a 3 s pause, up to 3 attempts total. The returned `GateResult` keeps the last attempt's output and sets `attempts`. Other failures run exactly once. Timeouts are not retried. `run_gates` (line ~114, stops at first failure) keeps the 3 s default; introduce an internal runner that takes a delay parameter so tests do not wait 3 s per retry. Tests use a scripted command (a small script or shell one-liner that prints `LNK1104` a fixed number of times), never a real linker. Write tests first in `crates/asf-vcs/tests/gates.rs`.

acceptance.text: `cargo test -p asf-vcs --test gates` covers: prints LNK1104 once then succeeds -> ok, attempts 2; always prints LNK1104 -> not ok, attempts 3; fails without LNK1104 -> attempts 1.
Public `run_gates` signature unchanged; default delay is 3 s.
Gates from the brief pass for the whole workspace.

title: plan new: manifest-driven prompt stages and schemas
body: Refactor `crates/asf/src/commands/plan.rs`: resolve the active methodology through `commands::method` (`crates/asf/src/commands/method.rs`, `BUILTIN` at lines ~18-39, local manifests from `.factory/methodologies/<name>/` at ~149). Take `prompt` stages in manifest order; load each stage's prompt and schema from the methodology (embedded for builtins, from disk for local ones). Remove the four `include_str!` constants at `plan.rs:18-21`. The request builder (`plan.rs:297-306`) must receive the stage's prompt text instead of the constants. Existing `cli_plan` tests must pass UNCHANGED. Add a new test with a local methodology whose `idea-to-prd.md` differs from the builtin and assert the fake planner receives that text. No new stage kinds; do not touch spec-kit or superpowers manifests. Write the new test first (RED).

acceptance.text: `cargo test -p asf --test cli_plan` passes; pre-existing tests are not edited.
New test: local methodology with custom `idea-to-prd.md` -> fake planner receives that exact text.
`grep include_str` in `plan.rs` returns nothing for the four prompt/schema constants.
Gates from the brief pass for the whole workspace.

title: Language line in planner prompts via {{language}} placeholder
body: Read `[methodology] language` from the active manifest (default `en`) in `crates/asf/src/commands/plan.rs` (available after task 7 refactor). Render a `Language: <code>` line into both prompts through a `{{language}}` placeholder added to `methodologies/asf-default/prompts/idea-to-prd.md` and `methodologies/asf-default/prompts/prd-to-issues.md`. Do not change spec-kit or superpowers manifests. Decision on open question 1: 'byte-for-byte identical' means identical to the post-change rendering; the language line is the only intended difference from the pre-change asf-default rendering. Write the test first in `crates/asf/tests/cli_plan.rs`: fake planner receives a prompt containing `Language: en`.

acceptance.text: `cargo test -p asf --test cli_plan` asserts the rendered prompt contains `Language: en` for both stages.
A manifest with `language = "pl"` renders `Language: pl`; missing key renders `en`.
Prompt diff versus pre-change asf-default is exactly the language placeholder/line.
Gates from the brief pass for the whole workspace.

title: Dogfooding round 2: unattended operator loop
body: Round 1 of dogfooding showed four gaps an operator had to close by hand: a run with a flaky failed verification could only be queued with `merge enqueue --force`; a merge could leave `main` red without anyone noticing; `asf serve` never stopped, so an external script drove the loop; and `asf repo init` did not ignore `.factory/plan/`. This epic closes those gaps with four independently mergeable increments: `asf run verify <id>` reruns worker verification and enqueues on success (T1); with `[merge] verify_main_after = true`, gates run in the repo root after every merge and a red `main` is recorded and reported without auto-revert (T2); `asf serve --until-done [--max-ticks N]` stops on `all_done`, `max_ticks` or `stuck` with a JSON summary (T3, after T1 because both touch `cli.rs`); and `repo init` / `repo doctor` manage the `.factory/plan/` ignore lines (T4). Non-goals: no trait changes in `ports.rs`, no Cargo manifest or lockfile changes, no automatic revert, no automatic retry, no TUI or worker-prompt work. `verify_main_after` defaults to false.

title: Add `asf run verify <id>` to rerun worker verification
body:
Goal: an operator can rerun the same verification that `asf run watch` performs after a worker finishes, without `merge enqueue --force`.

What to build:
1. In `crates/asf/src/worker.rs` expose the existing private verification routine as `pub fn verify_issue(&self, id: &IssueId) -> Result<Transition, AppError>`. Reuse the existing gate logic; do not duplicate it.
2. In `crates/asf/src/cli.rs` (near `RunCmd`, currently line ~410) add `RunCmd::Verify { id }`. Dispatch it from `crates/asf/src/commands/run.rs`. Run `grep -rn "RunCmd::" crates/` and fix every exhaustive match.
3. State checks run before any gate, using the exact messages and exit code 3 (conflict):
   - no run for the issue: "no run to verify"
   - run `succeeded`: "already verified and queued"
   - run `starting`, `working` or `blocked`: "worker still active; wait for `asf issue finish` or `asf run abort`"
   - run `aborted`: "run was aborted; dispatch again"
   - allowed states: `failed`, `finishing`, `verifying`.
4. On success: run moves to `succeeded` and the branch is enqueued in the merge queue, the same as `watch` does.
5. On failure: run stays `failed`, the new failure reason is stored in the run record, and a BLOCKER comment is posted on the issue.
6. Keep the existing refusal when the command is executed from inside a worker run.

Tests: add integration tests (new file `crates/asf/tests/cli_verify.rs` or extend `crates/asf/tests/cli_run.rs`) using a gate that fails, is then fixed, and a verify that succeeds and enqueues the branch.

acceptance.text: Integration test: a gate fails, is fixed, then `asf run verify <id>` succeeds; the run is `succeeded` and the branch is in the merge queue.
One test per refusal message (no run, succeeded, active states, aborted); each asserts exit code 3 and the exact message text.
A verify invoked from inside a worker run is still refused as before.
`cargo test -p asf` passes and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

title: Run gates on the repo root after merges when `verify_main_after` is set
body:
Goal: detect a red `main` right after a merge instead of only in worktrees.

What to build:
1. In `crates/asf-core/src/config.rs` add `verify_main_after: bool` to `MergeCfg` (struct at line ~186, `#[serde(default)]`, default `false`). Update the manual `Default` impl (line ~197) and any TOML fixture test (line ~307) if needed.
2. After a successful local fast-forward in the merge tick, and after `pull_ff` on the GitHub path (merged PR), run the configured gates in the repository root using `asf_vcs::gates::run_gates(specs, root)`. The GitHub path lives in `crates/asf/src/commands/merge.rs` and/or `crates/asf/src/commands/gh.rs`; check both. Gates run regardless of `require_clean_main` (decision recorded for open question 2).
3. On a red result:
   - set the item's `last_error` to "main red after merge: gate `<name>` failed (exit <code>)"
   - keep the item in `merged`
   - post a BLOCKER comment on the issue with the last 15 lines of the failing gate output and the commit SHA
   - append a `merge.main_red` event to the event log
   - stop processing further queue items in this tick, so any other queued item stays `queued`.
4. With the flag off (default) no gate runs and behaviour is unchanged. No automatic revert.

Do not change the `Vcs` trait or `crates/asf-core/src/ports.rs`.

acceptance.text: With `verify_main_after = true`, a shell gate that fails only in the repo root: the merged item is `merged` with `last_error` set, a `merge.main_red` event is in the event log, and a second queued item is still `queued`.
With the flag off (default), the same scenario leaves the item unchanged: no `last_error`, no `merge.main_red` event, no gate run.
The GitHub `pull_ff` path is covered with the FakeGitHub test double from `asf-vcs`.
`cargo test --workspace` passes and clippy with `-D warnings` is clean.

title: Add `asf serve --until-done [--max-ticks N]`
body:
Goal: `asf serve` can run unattended and stop on its own, printing a JSON summary.

What to build:
1. In `crates/asf/src/cli.rs` (`ServeArgs`, line ~105) add `--until-done` with `conflicts_with = "once"`, and `--max-ticks <N>` with `requires = "until_done"` (decision: `--max-ticks` without `--until-done` is a usage error). Task 1 also edits `cli.rs`, so this task starts after it.
2. In `crates/asf/src/commands/serve.rs` the loop stops on one of three reasons, checked after each tick:
   - `all_done`: no open non-epic issue remains. Exit 0.
   - `max_ticks`: N ticks have run. Exit 0.
   - `stuck`: open issues remain, no run is in `starting|working|finishing|verifying`, no merge item is in `queued|rebasing|gating|merging|pr_open`, and the allocation plan (see `crates/asf-core/src/scheduler.rs`, read-only) has no slot. `blocked`, `stalled` and `over_budget` runs count as stuck. One stuck tick is enough (decision for open question 3).
3. Per-tick output is unchanged. With `--until-done` print only ticks that had events.
4. Final result is `{ "ticks", "reason", "open", "runs" }` inside the normal `{"ok":true,"result":...}` envelope. `all_done` and `max_ticks` exit 0. `stuck` exits 3 with `ok:true` and `reason: "stuck"` as written in the spec (decision for open question 1; the `ok:false` envelope stays for errors only).

Tests go in `crates/asf/tests/cli_serve.rs`.

acceptance.text: `asf serve --until-done` on a finished set: `reason` is `all_done` after one tick, exit 0.
An open issue with empty `file_scope` and nothing running: `reason` is `stuck`, exit 3, envelope `ok` is true.
`asf serve --until-done --max-ticks 2` with work remaining: `reason` is `max_ticks`, `ticks` is 2, exit 0.
`asf serve --once --until-done` fails with a clap usage error (exit 2).
`cargo test -p asf --test cli_serve` passes and the workspace clippy gate is clean.

title: Ignore `.factory/plan/` in `repo init` and report it in `repo doctor`
body:
Goal: planner artifacts under `.factory/plan/` are never committed, and `doctor` says when that is not the case.

What to build:
1. In `crates/asf/src/commands/repo.rs` add `.factory/plan/` to `IGNORE_LINES` (line ~18). `repo init` already writes through `ensure_lines` to both `.gitignore` and `.git/info/exclude` (lines ~92-95); keep the writes idempotent.
2. In `crates/asf/src/commands/doctor.rs` add a `gitignore` check:
   - `ok` when every `IGNORE_LINES` entry is present in at least one of the two files (`.gitignore` or `.git/info/exclude`)
   - otherwise `warn`, with the missing lines listed in `detail` and the hint "run `asf repo init` to add them"
   - if neither file exists, `warn` (decision for open question 4)
   - the check never produces `fail`.
3. Follow the existing check shape in `doctor.rs` for the output struct.

Non-goals: no changes to the `IssueStore` trait or any Cargo manifest.

acceptance.text: Running `repo init` on an existing repo adds `.factory/plan/` exactly once to `.gitignore` and to `.git/info/exclude`; a second run changes neither file.
`repo doctor` reports `gitignore` `ok` when all lines are ignored and `warn` with the missing lines in `detail` plus the hint otherwise; it never reports `fail`.
`cargo test -p asf --test cli_repo` passes and the workspace clippy gate is clean.

title: Dogfooding round 3: review gate, human questions, validating status, config editing
body: Round 3 of the asf dogfooding closes four gaps found in round 2. Workers write open questions into report.md where nobody reads them, so finish must be refused while a QUESTION to the human is unanswered, and reports with an open-questions section fail verification. The [review] config is never read by the merge queue, so a reviewer gate is added: a green merge item with review required enters reviewing, runs a read-only reviewer in a detached worktree, and merges only on approve, with a bounded number of change rounds. A validating status sits between in-review and done, backed by a schema v2 migration that upgrades v1 databases in place. Configuration becomes editable through a comment-preserving `asf config show|set` command and a Config view in the TUI, built on a toml_edit-based config_edit module that validates before writing. Gates gain a `when` field to select verify, merge or main stages. Open questions from the PRD (foreign_keys during migration, DECISION authorship, round counting, gate default, dirty main during review, stale config during serve) need the defaults stated in the task bodies; the tasks adopt the PRD's stated defaults and flag the rest for review.

title: Add validating status and schema v2 migration
body:
Goal: introduce Status::Validating and an in-place v1 -> v2 database migration for issues.status.

What to build:
- In crates/asf-core/src/model.rs add Validating ("validating") to the str_enum! between InReview and Done. Status::ALL keeps board order. is_terminal is unchanged.
- Bump the schema to version 2 (crates/asf-store/src/schema.sql has CHECK (status IN (...)) on issues.status and must include 'validating').
- In crates/asf-store/src/lib.rs, SqliteStore::migrate() currently only runs SCHEMA_SQL when the meta table is absent. Add a v1 -> v2 step: turn foreign_keys OFF on the connection before the transaction (PRAGMA is a no-op inside a transaction), then in one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction create issues_new with the new CHECK, copy rows, drop issues, rename issues_new to issues, commit, then turn foreign_keys back ON. Assumption adopted for PRD open question 1: disable FKs for the whole rebuild window, not per statement. Recreate any indexes on issues.
- crates/asf/src/commands/doctor.rs checks the schema version with v == 1; accept the version-2 constant instead.
- Exhaustive matches on Status outside asf-core/asf-store (for example in crates/asf/src/tui/view.rs) must get the minimal new arm so the workspace compiles; do not add the Board column itself (that is Task 7).

TDD: write failing tests first (RED), then the minimal change (GREEN).

Tests:
- A v1 database (create it with the old schema SQL in the test) is opened with the new code, reaches version 2, and keeps its issues rows, comments rows and runs rows that reference issues.
- issues.jsonl export and import round-trip an issue with status validating.

Repo conventions: thiserror in libraries, UTF-8 text, RFC 3339 UTC timestamps. Do not touch the IssueStore trait in crates/asf-core/src/ports.rs. No general migration framework: only this one step.

acceptance.text: cargo test -p asf-store passes, including a test that migrates a v1 database and keeps issues, comments and runs rows
A database created with the v1 schema reports schema version 2 after open and its row counts are unchanged
Exporting and re-importing issues.jsonl preserves an issue with status validating
asf doctor accepts a version-2 database without a warning
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings passes

title: Config: reviewer model, gate stages, and comment-preserving config_edit module
body:
Goal: extend the config model and add the editing engine used by the CLI (Task 4) and the TUI (Task 7).

What to build:
- crates/asf-core/src/config.rs: ReviewCfg gains model: String (default "opus") and max_rounds: u32 (default 2). GateCfg gains when: Vec<GateWhen>, where enum GateWhen { Verify, Merge, Main } uses lowercase serde names and an absent field defaults to all three stages (PRD open question 4 resolved to the PRD's stated default). TEMPLATE gets commented examples for the new keys.
- New module crates/asf-core/src/config_edit.rs, exported from crates/asf-core/src/lib.rs: set_key(toml: &str, key: &str, value: &str) -> Result<String, ConfigError> and editable_keys() -> &[(&str, &str)] covering exactly the ten keys named in the PRD brief. Use the toml_edit crate (latest 0.2x) for the edit so comments, ordering and unrelated content survive. The value is parsed as a TOML scalar or array and falls back to a plain string. The result must pass Config::from_toml, otherwise return an error and write nothing. A missing section is created.
- Add toml_edit to [workspace.dependencies] in the root Cargo.toml and to crates/asf-core/Cargo.toml. This is the only new crate. Only this task touches Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock.
- ConfigError is a thiserror enum in asf-core.

TDD: write failing tests first (RED), then the minimal change (GREEN).

Tests (crates/asf-core/tests/config_edit.rs):
- Comments and key order survive a set of an existing key.
- scheduler.max_parallel = 0 is refused and the input string is unchanged (caller writes nothing).
- A missing section such as [review] is created.
- A gate with when = ["verify"] parses and an absent when yields all three stages.

acceptance.text: cargo test -p asf-core config_edit passes
Setting an existing key in a commented config file keeps every comment line and key order
set_key with scheduler.max_parallel = 0 returns an error and the caller's config text is not changed
set_key on a key whose section is missing creates the section
Config::from_toml accepts a config with review.model, review.max_rounds and gate.when, and defaults are opus, 2 and all three stages
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings passes

title: Rewrite worker protocol and add review brief with verdict parser
body:
Goal: change what workers are told about questions and finishing, and add the brief and verdict parser the reviewer needs.

What to build in crates/asf-core/src/brief.rs:
- Rewrite the ## Protocol and ## Finish ritual sections so that: blocking questions go through AskUserQuestion; non-blocking questions go through `asf issue comment --type QUESTION --to human`; the report has no open-questions section; deviations are posted as `DECISION --to human`; `asf issue finish` is refused while a QUESTION to human is unanswered.
- Add ReviewInput and render_review_brief. The reviewer must diff against base_sha, check each acceptance criterion, run the gates, never edit files, and end its output with exactly one DECISION comment whose first line is `approve` or `changes:` followed by bullets.
- Add enum Verdict { Approve, Changes(Vec<String>) } and parse_verdict(&str) -> Option<Verdict>. The first line is matched case-insensitively. Garbage input returns None.

TDD: write failing tests first (RED), then the minimal change (GREEN).

Tests (crates/asf-core/tests/brief.rs and/or unit tests in brief.rs):
- Rendered worker brief contains the required phrases (AskUserQuestion, --type QUESTION --to human, DECISION --to human, finish refused).
- Rendered review brief contains base_sha, the gate commands and the approve/changes instruction, and does not mention editing as allowed.
- parse_verdict handles approve, changes: with bullet findings, mixed case, and returns None on garbage.

acceptance.text: cargo test -p asf-core brief passes
The rendered worker brief contains AskUserQuestion, `--type QUESTION --to human` and `DECISION --to human`, and says finish is refused while a QUESTION is unanswered
render_review_brief output mentions base_sha, every acceptance criterion and the single final DECISION rule
parse_verdict returns Approve for approve, Changes with the bullets for changes:, and None for garbage text
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings passes

title: Add asf config show and asf config set CLI commands
body:
Goal: expose the config_edit module on the command line.

What to build:
- crates/asf/src/cli.rs: Cmd::Config { cmd: ConfigCmd } with subcommands Show and Set { key, value }.
- crates/asf/src/commands/config.rs (new), registered in crates/asf/src/commands/mod.rs and dispatched from crates/asf/src/main.rs.
- Show prints the current values of editable_keys() from .factory/config.toml.
- Set calls config_edit::set_key, writes UTF-8 without BOM and LF line endings, and prints old and new values. The success text reads "restart `asf serve` to apply". An unknown key or an invalid value exits 1 and leaves the file untouched.
- Refused inside a worker run: reuse the same guard that other mutating commands use (check crates/asf/src/commands/issue.rs and crates/asf/src/worker.rs for the existing worker-run detection) and do not invent a new environment variable.
- --json envelope {"ok":true,"result":...} / {"ok":false,"error":{...}} on both subcommands; exit codes 0/1/2.

title: Worker finish guard, report verification, and review worktree start
body:
Goal: refuse finish while a human QUESTION is open, make verification validate the report, and create the review issue and its detached worktree.

Edit and Write are NOT allowed.

title: Merge queue gate stages and reviewer decision handling
body:
Goal: make the merge queue honour gate.when and run the reviewer gate before merging.

What to build in the merge queue (crates/asf/src/commands/merge.rs, gate execution in crates/asf-vcs/src/gates.rs):
- Gates run after rebase only when when contains merge. Post-merge root gates run only when when contains main. Absent when means all three (PRD default).
- After green gates, when [review] required is true or an on_labels label is present on the issue, the item enters reviewing. The first tick calls Worker::start_review and returns.
- Later ticks read the newest DECISION from the review issue (author: the review issue id, per the Task 5 assumption):
  - approve: continue to fast-forward or PR as today.
  - changes: set the item to failed with the findings in last_error, set the original issue to blocked, post a BLOCKER to the human. If the original run is still alive, also send a run reply carrying the findings.
  - Round counting: count changes DECISIONs on the original issue; when the count reaches [review] max_rounds (2), stop with a BLOCKER asking the human to decide instead of starting another reviewer. (Assumption for PRD open question 3.)
  - No DECISION yet: stay in reviewing silently.
- Dirty main while in reviewing: the item stays parked in reviewing with a log line (assumption for PRD open question 5).
- On merged: the original issue moves from validating to done and the review issue is closed done. Its worktree is left for lane clean.

title: Dogfooding round 4: no operator steps
body: Round 3 of dogfooding required nine operator interventions: four `asf run abort` after a false start timeout, two `asf run verify` after a worker fixed a failed run, two `asf issue edit --scope` rewrites so workers could touch out-of-scope tests, and one loop restart. This epic removes those causes: test helpers stop leaking worker env vars (canary task for the newly required read-only reviewer), `Worker::start` retries a start timeout once, `watch` re-verifies fixed runs using only `verify` gates and reuses already-queued merge items, workers can request scope extensions through a new `asf issue scope add/rm` flow, `asf serve` hot-reloads config and reports `questions_waiting`, reviewer approvals survive retries on an identical patch (patch-id fingerprint), and the TUI shows a waiting count and can unset optional config keys. No changes to Cargo manifests, `ports.rs`, the Herdr adapter, GitHub sync or planner prompts.

title: TUI: waiting agents are obvious and answerable; unset optional config keys
body:
Part A (`crates/asf/src/tui/`): the header shows 'N waiting' in accent style when N > 0, where N = unanswered QUESTIONs to `human` + runs in `blocked`, computed inside the TUI snapshot (do not depend on task 5 code). Part B: in the Config view, pressing `d` on `worker.model` or `review.model` asks 'unset <key>? y' and, on confirmation, removes the key. Add `pub fn unset_key(toml: &str, key: &str) -> Result<String, ConfigError>` to `crates/asf-core/src/config_edit.rs` (no IO): it preserves other comments/formatting (follow the approach already used by `set_key` in that file), refuses required keys with a `ConfigError`, and its output must pass `Config::from_toml`.

Part C (operator feedback, 2026-11-05: "questions asked with AskUserQuestion work, but the TUI does not show clearly that an agent is asking"). Make a waiting agent impossible to miss and answerable from the TUI:

1. Banner: when N > 0, one line directly under the tab bar, bold and in the warning style, visible in every view: `■ asf-27 is waiting for your answer · a answer · f focus pane` for a run in `blocked`, or `■ asf-27 asks: <first line of the QUESTION body, truncated>` for an unanswered QUESTION comment to `human`. With several, show the oldest and ` (+K more)`. No banner when N = 0 (the layout must not jump for other reasons: reserve the line only while N > 0).
2. Markers: on the Board a card whose run is `blocked` shows `■ ?` (bold, red) instead of `▶`; in the Agents table the row of a `blocked` run starts with `■` and is bold red. A working run keeps `▶`. Never rely on colour alone: the symbol differs too.
3. Answer overlay: key `a` on a selected issue (Board, Agents, Inbox) that has a `blocked` run opens a centred modal titled `answer asf-27`. Opening it triggers a new `Action::Peek(id)`; `tui/mod.rs` reads the last 20 lines of the worker pane through the runtime (`rt.read`, as `Worker::watch` does for the BLOCKER) and stores them in the app state so the modal shows the question and its numbered options. Inside the modal: digits `1`-`9`, `Enter`, `Up`, `Down` are sent to the worker pane as keys (existing `Worker::keys`), `t` switches to a text input whose content is sent with `Worker::reply`, `Esc` closes without sending anything. After sending, close the modal and show `sent <keys> to asf-27` in the status line. While the modal is open no other binding is active (digits must not switch views).
4. Remove the bare `y` / `n` passthrough from normal mode (today they send keys to the selected worker without showing what is being answered); `y`/`n` remain available inside the answer overlay like any other key. Update the footer hint list: replace `y/n keys` with `a answer`.

Read current ratatui docs before touching rendering/key handling (centred modal: `Clear` widget + a `Rect` computed with `Layout`/`Flex::Center`). Do not edit `commands/config.rs`. TDD.

title: TUI: fix five audit defects and add a key reference (help view)
body:
Five TUI defects found by the UX audit of 2026-11-05, plus the key reference the operator asked for ("there are a lot of keys already, give me a view that lists them"). Everything lives in `crates/asf/src/tui/`; item 2 needs one small store method. asf-30 lands first (banner, answer overlay): build on it, do not undo it.

1. Status message expires. `app.status` is set after every action and never cleared, so the key hints in the footer disappear for good after the first action. A status message is shown for 4 seconds or until the next key press, then the footer shows the hints again. Keep `app.rs` pure: pass the clock in (for example a tick counter or an `Instant` supplied by `tui/mod.rs`).

2. Inbox: Enter opens, marking read is explicit. Today Enter marks the WHOLE inbox read although the title says "Enter = mark read". New behaviour: `Enter` opens a modal with the full comment (wrapped, scrollable with j/k, header line `#id issue [author] TYPE -> to`, `Esc` closes); `m` marks the conversation of the selected comment's issue as read (every unread comment on that issue for the `human` lane); `M` asks `mark all N read? y` and only then marks everything. Add the store method for the per-issue case: `fn mark_read(&self, lane: &str, issue: &IssueId) -> Result<usize, StoreError>` on `IssueStore` (`crates/asf-core/src/ports.rs`; the `cursors(lane, issue_id, last_comment_id)` table already keeps a cursor per issue), implemented in `asf-store` with a test. Run `grep -rn "impl IssueStore" crates/` and implement it for every implementor.

3. Long actions do not freeze the screen. `t` (tick) and `s` (start worker) run synchronously in the UI thread today: a tick can run the gates for minutes and a start blocks for up to 180 s with no redraw. Run them as child processes of the current executable (`std::env::current_exe()`): `asf --repo <root> serve --once --json` for the tick and `asf --repo <root> run start <id> --json` for the start, polled with `try_wait` from the event loop. While one runs, the header shows a braille spinner and a label (`⠋ tick…`, `⠋ starting asf-25…`) and every key keeps working. When it exits, show `✓ <summary>` or `✗ <error message from the JSON envelope>` as the status message. One background action at a time: a second request answers `busy: <label>`. Killing the TUI must not leave the terminal broken (the child inherits nothing interactive: stdin null, stdout/stderr piped).

4. Ctrl+C and control keys. `Ctrl+C` quits from any mode. In the text input `Ctrl+U` clears the line and `Ctrl+W` deletes the last word. A key event with the CONTROL or ALT modifier never inserts a character.

5. Contextual footer. One table of bindings (key, action label, the views and modes where it applies) is the single source for the footer and the help view. The footer shows at most 7 hints for the current view and mode, formatted `key action` with the key bold and the action dim, always ending with `? help` and `q quit`, and it must fit in 100 columns (test every view at width 100).

6. Help view. `?` opens a full-screen overlay listing every binding from that table, grouped: Global, Navigation, Board, Agents, Inbox, Queue, Config, Answer overlay. Each line is `key  what it does` in plain words (for example `m  mark this issue's messages as read`). Scroll with j/k, close with `Esc`, `?` or `q`. While it is open no other binding is active.

7. Conventional navigation, since the table makes it cheap: `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` cycle the views, `g` / `G` jump to the first / last row, `Esc` in normal mode closes the Board detail panel.

Tests in `crates/asf/src/tui/tests.rs`: status expiry; Enter opens the comment modal and does not change the unread count; `m` yields the per-issue action; `M` needs `y`; Ctrl+C quits from input mode; Ctrl+W/Ctrl+U editing; footer fits 100 columns in every view and differs between Board and Config; `?` opens help and blocks other keys; Tab cycles. `crates/asf/tests/cli_tui.rs`: `asf tui --once` still renders. Store test for `mark_read`. Read the current ratatui and crossterm docs (key modifiers, `Clear`, scrolling a `Paragraph`) before writing calls. TDD.

title: TUI: Now view, the operator's desk
body:
A new first view, `Now`: the operator's desk. Today the TUI opens on the Board, which answers "which issues exist". The operator opens it with a different question: "does the factory need something from me, and if not, what is it doing". Build the view from this mockup (120 columns):

```
 asf · auto-software-factory · main      ● runtime   workers 1/2   ⚠ 2 waiting   ⠋ merging asf-24
 Now   Board   Agents   Inbox   Queue   Log   Config
 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  NEEDS YOU (2)
  ▸ ■ asf-27  question      Keep the old --scope flag as an alias?        4 min   a answer
    ■ asf-25  merge failed  gate `test` after rebase (2 tests)            12 min  v verify

  RUNNING (2)
    ● asf-24  working       Strip worker env vars from cli_export tests   $0.50 / $10   6 min
    ◆ asf-31  review        opus · round 1                                $0.21         1 min

  UP NEXT (6)   asf-25, asf-27, asf-28 … waiting for asf-24
  DONE TODAY (7)   ✓ asf-22  ✓ asf-21  ✓ asf-20  ✓ asf-19 …
 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  j/k move   a answer   f focus pane   Enter open issue   Tab next view   ? help   q quit
```

Rules:
- `View::Now` is the first view and the default of `asf tui`; the views are now Now, Board, Agents, Inbox, Queue, Log, Config on keys `1`-`7` (`--view now` works; update the bindings table and help from asf-31).
- NEEDS YOU lists, oldest first: runs in `blocked` (label `question`, text = first non-empty line of the worker screen captured in the latest BLOCKER comment, or "waiting for your answer"), unanswered QUESTION comments to `human` (label `question`, first line of the body), runs in `failed`, `stalled` or `over_budget` (label = the state, text = first line of the exit reason), merge items in `failed` or `blocked` (label `merge failed` / `merge blocked`, first line of `last_error`). Each row ends with its age and the one key that acts on it: `a answer` (the overlay from asf-30), `v verify` (reruns verification through the background-action mechanism of asf-31: `asf run verify <id>`), `r retry` (`asf merge retry <id>`, same mechanism). When the section is empty it reads `Nothing needs you.` in the dim style.
- RUNNING lists active runs including reviewer runs: symbol, issue id, state (a reviewer shows `review` and the model), title, cost / budget, elapsed time. Empty: `No worker is running. Press Tab for the Board to start one.`
- UP NEXT is one line: the count of `ready` + `backlog` issues, the first ids, and what they wait for when they share one dependency. DONE TODAY is one line of ids closed today (local date), newest first, truncated with `…`.

title: Workers and reviewers start Claude Code with a readable session name
body:
Operator request (2026-11-05): sessions started by asf are only identifiable by their UUID in Claude Code's session list and in /resume. Claude Code has '-n, --name <name>' (verified with claude --help, 2.1.318): 'Set a display name for this session'. In crates/asf/src/worker.rs, where the worker arguments are built (next to --permission-mode, --session-id and --model, around line 449), add --name <value> for worker runs and for reviewer runs (start_review). Value: '<issue-id>-<slug of the title>' for a worker and 'review-<reviewed-issue-id>-<slug>' for a reviewer; the slug is lowercase ASCII letters and digits with single hyphens, the whole value at most 60 characters and without spaces (arguments are typed into a shell by the runtime, so no spaces and no quotes). Example: asf-27-add-asf-issue-scope-add-rm-and-scope-request. A title with no ASCII letters yields just the id. Put the slug function next to the other pure helpers and unit-test it (unicode title, very long title, punctuation only). Extend the existing argument tests in worker.rs / crates/asf/tests/cli_run.rs: the fake runtime's recorded start arguments contain --name with the expected value for a worker and for a reviewer. Do not change the session id or the agent name used by Herdr. TDD.

Also (operator report, 2026-11-05): Claude Code 2.1.318 prints `Deny rule MultiEdit matches no tool - check for typos` in every reviewer pane, because the `MultiEdit` tool no longer exists. Remove `MultiEdit` from `REVIEW_DENY` in crates/asf/src/worker.rs (keep Edit, Write, NotebookEdit) and from the test that lists the denied tools. Leave the hook matchers in brief.rs and hook.rs alone (out of scope; a matcher for a missing tool is harmless).

title: TUI: per-view modules, shared theme and chrome, richer snapshot
body:
Foundation for the TUI redesign. After round 4 the whole TUI is two big files (`tui/app.rs`, `tui/view.rs`); six view tasks follow this one and must be able to run in parallel on disjoint files. Restructure without changing what the user sees, except that the two overlays are brought in line with their mockups.

Target layout of `crates/asf/src/tui/`:
- `theme.rs`: the symbols and every `Style` (bold, dim, accent, ok, warn, danger, selected row), with `NO_COLOR` handled in one place.
- `chrome.rs`: header line, tab bar, waiting banner, footer hints, the horizontal rules, the too-small gate. Nothing else draws those rows.
- `bindings.rs`: the single table of key bindings (key, plain-words description, footer label, where it applies) that feeds the footer and the help view. Each view contributes its own `BINDINGS` constant.
- `overlays.rs`: answer overlay, help view, comment modal, confirmation, text input.
- `snapshot.rs`: `Snapshot` and its loading (moved from `mod.rs`), plus pure helpers shared by views.
- `views/{now,board,agents,inbox,queue,log,config}.rs`: each with `pub struct State` (selection, scroll, filter, folds), `pub fn render(frame: &mut Frame, area: Rect, snap: &Snapshot, state: &State, theme: &Theme)`, `pub fn handle_key(key: KeyEvent, snap: &Snapshot, state: &mut State) -> Action` and `pub const BINDINGS`.
- `app.rs`: `App` (current view, the seven states, overlay stack, status message) and the dispatch only.
- `tests/<name>.rs`: the existing tests moved next to what they test.

Extend the snapshot so the view tasks need no IO changes:
- `deps`: every dependency edge (issue, depends on).
- `last_runs`: the latest run of every issue, finished ones included (state, cost, budget, tool calls, started and finished times, model, pane, session name when known).
- `merged_today`: merge items merged today (local date) with head sha.
- `review_of`: review issue id to the issue it reviews (the review issue's parent), and the review round from the `merge.review_started` events.
- `needs_you`: one list used by the header count, the banner, the Now view and the Inbox: blocked runs, unanswered QUESTIONs to `human`, runs in failed / stalled / over_budget, merge items failed / blocked, each with issue id, kind, one-line text, age and the action key.
- `detail`: comments and dependency status of the issue selected on the Board, loaded on demand through an `Action::LoadDetail(id)`; `pane_preview`: the last lines of a worker pane, loaded through the existing peek action.

Overlays: make the answer overlay and the help view look like these mockups (centred box with an accent border for the answer overlay; two columns of grouped bindings for help, generated from the bindings table, with the symbols legend at the bottom).

title: TUI: Inbox split into Needs you and For your information
body:
Rebuild the Inbox. Today 62 unread comments of every kind are one flat list and a linker dump takes six lines.

- NEEDS YOU (count): the items of the snapshot's `needs_you` list. Each item: symbol, issue id, kind (QUESTION, BLOCKER), age, one line of text, and under it a dim line with what to do and the keys that do it (`a answer`; for a failed merge `Enter full output · v verify again · r reply to the worker`). A BLOCKER caused by a failed gate is summarised: first line `Merge failed: gate <name> after rebase` or `Verification failed: gate <name>`, second line the names of the failed tests parsed from the comment body (the lines listed under `failures:`), or the first error line when there are none.
- FOR YOUR INFORMATION (count unread): every other unread comment relevant to the human, newest first, one line each: symbol by kind (`✓` merged FYI, `◆` DECISION, `●` STATUS), issue id, kind, age, first line of the body.
- `A` toggles `show everything (N)`: the flat chronological list of all unread comments, one line each.
- Keys: `j`/`k`, `Enter` opens the comment modal, `a` answer, `v` verify, `r` reply, `m` mark this issue's messages read, `M` mark all read (asks first).
- Empty: `Nothing needs you and nothing new to read.`

body:
Rebuild the Log view. Today each line is an event kind and a raw JSON payload.

title: Capacity: worker slots count working workers; reviewers get their own limit
body: Operator observation (2026-11-05, round 4): with [scheduler] max_parallel = 2 and [review] required = true the factory runs almost serially. An issue under review holds two slots: its own claim stays until the merge (the worker is finished, the issue is validating) and the reviewer takes a second claim. Operator decision: reviews do not count against the worker limit and have a limit of their own. Change: (1) capacity for new workers = [scheduler] max_parallel minus the number of worker runs that are active (run state starting, working, blocked, finishing or verifying on an issue whose type is not review). A claim without an active run (an issue in validating waiting for review or merge, a run that already succeeded) does not take a slot. Scope conflicts must still consider every claimed issue, including those waiting in validating, because their branch is not merged yet: only the counting changes. Find where the count comes from (SchedulerInput in crates/asf-core/src/scheduler.rs and current_plan in crates/asf/src/commands/run.rs pass claims today) and add what is needed to tell an active worker run from a held claim. (2) New [review] max_parallel: u32, default 2, minimum 1 (validated), with a commented line in the config TEMPLATE. In crates/asf/src/commands/merge.rs, before a reviewer is started for an item, count the reviewer runs that are active; when the limit is reached the item stays as it is (gates already green) and the review starts on a later tick, without failing the item and without a comment. Order is FIFO by merge item id. (3) asf run plan shows both numbers in its header: workers running / max and reviewers running / max. Tests: scheduler unit tests for an issue in validating with a held claim not consuming a slot while still blocking a conflicting scope; a CLI test where two verified items wait and [review] max_parallel = 1 starts one reviewer at a time; config default and validation. TDD.

title: Reviewer brief: read the change, run only the tests the criteria need
body: Operator decision (2026-11-06). In round 4 every review took about 25 minutes and cost more than a small change: the reviewer built the project from scratch in its detached worktree and ran the whole gate set, although the merge queue had run every gate on that exact commit a moment earlier (a review only starts after the gates are green). Change the review brief in crates/asf-core/src/brief.rs (render_review_brief): (1) say plainly that the full gates (formatter, linter, complete test suite) already passed in the merge queue on this commit after the rebase, that the reviewer must not rerun the whole suite, and that its job is to read the diff against the issue text and every acceptance criterion; (2) the reviewer runs only targeted commands that prove an acceptance criterion or probe a suspicion (a single test, one test file, one package), and names in the verdict what it ran; (3) it still never edits; (4) the verdict comment is addressed to the reviewed issue, not to the human: asf issue comment <reviewed-id> --type DECISION --to <reviewed-id> --body "approve" (or "changes:" with findings). In round 4 the brief said --to orchestrator, which the CLI does not accept as an addressee, so reviewers fell back to --to human and every approve landed in the operator inbox; the merge queue reads verdicts by author, so the addressee does not matter to it. Keep parse_verdict unchanged. Update the tests of the rendered review brief (the sentences about gates already passed, targeted tests only, and the exact comment command with the reviewed id as addressee). TDD.

title: fix(vcs): wait out a linker lock when there is no file to move aside
body:
## Problem

On Windows the gate runner already reruns a gate when the only failure evidence is a linker lock
(`LNK1104`) and moves the locked executable aside first (`crates/asf-vcs/src/gates.rs`,
`run_gate_with_retry`, `move_locked_aside`). On 2026-11-06 two merge items (asf-47, asf-31) still
failed in the `test` gate after all 5 attempts. The gate tail of both shows:

```
LINK : fatal error LNK1104: nie można otworzyć pliku "D:\...\.worktrees\asf-47\target\debug\deps\asf_vcs-8cd7fc69d49f91f7.exe"
[asf] gate `test` hit a linker lock (LNK1104); moved aside []; rerun attempt 2/5
[asf] gate `test` hit a linker lock (LNK1104); moved aside []; rerun attempt 3/5
[asf] gate `test` hit a linker lock (LNK1104); moved aside []; rerun attempt 4/5
[asf] gate `test` hit a linker lock (LNK1104); moved aside []; rerun attempt 5/5
```

`moved aside []` every time: the file named by the linker does not exist on disk (checked after the
failure: no such `.exe` in `deps/`). So the linker cannot *create* the file (the antivirus scanner
still holds the name of a just-deleted executable), and there is nothing to move aside. The current
pauses (2 s, 4 s, 6 s, 8 s = 20 s in total) are too short for that case, and the message does not
say why nothing was moved.

## Wanted behaviour

1. When a rerun is caused by `LNK1104` and no locked file could be moved aside (none exists, or none
   could be parsed), wait noticeably longer before the rerun than in the "moved aside" case: the
   only remedy is time. Use a separate, longer pause schedule for this case (suggested: 15 s, 30 s,
   60 s, 60 s; keep the existing short schedule when a file was moved). Keep the total number of
   attempts at 5. The gate's own `timeout_s` applies per attempt, as today.
2. The note appended to the gate tail says which case happened, in plain words, for example
   `nothing to move aside (the file does not exist yet); waiting 30 s` instead of `moved aside []`.
3. The pause lengths must be injectable so tests do not sleep for minutes (for example a private
   function taking the schedule, with the public `run_gates` passing the real constants). Do not
   add a config key for this.
4. Behaviour for a locked file that exists (moved aside, short pause) stays exactly as it is, and
   so does the behaviour for failures without `LNK1104` (no rerun).

## Out of scope

- No change to `GateResult` fields, to config, or to how the merge queue reacts to a failed gate.
- No attempt to detect or configure the antivirus.

## Hints

- TDD: add the failing tests in `crates/asf-vcs/tests/gates.rs` first. The existing tests there use
  a small Python one-liner as the fake gate command; reuse that style (a gate that prints an
  `LNK1104` line naming a path that does not exist and passes on the N-th call, counted in a temp
  file).
- Windows note for your own test runs: if `cargo test` itself hits `LNK1104`, rerun it; that is the
  very problem this issue is about and not a defect in your change.

acceptance.text: an LNK1104 failure naming a file that does not exist is rerun after the longer pause schedule and the gate passes when a later attempt succeeds
the gate tail says in plain words that nothing could be moved aside and how long it waits; it no longer prints 'moved aside []'
a locked file that exists is still moved aside with the short pause; a failure without LNK1104 is not rerun
tests inject the pause schedule and the whole asf-vcs test suite still finishes in seconds

title: Gates: fix the flaky timeout_kills_and_reports test (gate runner returns late under parallel tests)
body:
## Problem

`crates/asf-vcs/tests/gates.rs::timeout_kills_and_reports` is flaky on Windows. Reviewer asf-55
observed on 2026-11-06 (main `d64779b`): `cargo test --workspace` and `cargo test -p asf-vcs
--no-fail-fast` fail in that test with the assertion `start.elapsed().as_secs() < 10` ("killed well
before 30 s"), while `cargo test -p asf-vcs --test gates timeout_kills_and_reports -- --exact`
passes in 1.1 s and `cargo test -p asf-vcs --test gates -- --test-threads=1` passes 18/18.

The test runs a gate `python -c "import time; time.sleep(30)"` with `timeout_s = 1` and expects
`run_gates` to return within 10 s. So with parallel test threads the gate runner needs 10 s or more
to return after a 1 s timeout.

## Wanted

1. Find the cause first (systematic debugging, no guessing). Candidates to check, not conclusions:
   the kill reaches only the direct child while a grandchild keeps the stdout/stderr pipe open and
   the output drain is joined after the kill; the timeout clock or the wait loop is starved by the
   linker-lock tests added in asf-51 that share the test binary; process start is slow under load
   and the timeout is measured from the wrong point.
2. If the gate runner itself can block after a timeout (for example on a pipe held by a
   grandchild), fix the runner: after the timeout the runner must return promptly even when a
   descendant of the gate command is still alive. Add a test that pins this.
3. If the runner is correct and only the test is fragile under parallel load, make the test robust
   without weakening what it proves (the gate is killed long before its own 30 s sleep ends and the
   result reports a timeout with no exit code).
4. `cargo test -p asf-vcs --test gates` must pass 20 times in a row with the default (parallel)
   test threads. State in the report how you checked this.

## Out of scope

- No change to `GateResult` fields or to config keys.
- No change to the linker-lock (`LNK1104`) retry behaviour.

## Hints

- Windows note for your own test runs: if `cargo test` itself hits `LNK1104`, rerun it; that is the
  antivirus and not a defect in your change.

acceptance.text: The cause of the late return is identified and stated in the report
After a gate timeout the runner returns promptly even when a descendant process is still alive, or the report shows the runner was already correct
cargo test -p asf-vcs --test gates passes 20 times in a row with parallel test threads
cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test --workspace pass

title: Merge: send review findings back to the idle worker and re-queue after its fix
body:
## Problem

When a reviewer answers `changes`, `request_changes` (`crates/asf/src/commands/merge.rs`) marks the
merge item `failed`, sets the issue `blocked` and posts a BLOCKER to the human. It sends the findings
to the worker only when the worker's run is still active. In practice the run is already
`succeeded` by then (the worker finished, the run was verified, the item was queued), so nothing is
sent, although the worker's pane is still open and idle in the runtime.

On 2026-11-06 this happened four times (asf-47, asf-31 twice, plus the earlier asf-30). Each time the
operator did by hand what the factory should do:

1. wrote the findings to `<worktree>/.factory/runs/<id>/review-<n>.md`,
2. sent the worker one line with `asf run reply <id> "... read .factory/runs/<id>/review-<n>.md ..."`,
3. waited for the worker's commit,
4. ran `asf merge retry <id>`.

## Wanted behaviour

1. On a `changes` verdict, while the number of `changes` rounds is below `[review] max_rounds`, and
   the worker's agent can still be reached in the runtime even though its run is no longer active:
   - write the findings to `<worktree>/.factory/runs/<id>/review-<round>.md` (round = number of
     `changes` verdicts so far; UTF-8, LF). The file says that the findings are data from the
     reviewer, lists them, and tells the worker to fix them test-first, run the gates, commit and
     finish again with `asf issue finish`;
   - send the worker a one-line prompt that points to that file (no findings inline: they can be
     long and contain quotes);
   - make the run workable again so that `asf issue finish <id>` is accepted and the normal
     finish -> verify path runs (reopen the run or start a new attempt on the same pane: your
     choice, state it in a DECISION comment). The issue goes back to `in-progress`;
   - post a STATUS comment to `all` instead of a BLOCKER to the human ("review round N asked for
     changes; findings sent to the worker").
2. When the worker finishes again and verification passes, the existing merge item is queued again
   without an operator command (asf-26 already reuses the item on enqueue), so the next tick
   rebases, runs the gates and starts the next review round.
3. When the worker cannot be reached (no pane, prompt delivery fails) the behaviour of today stays:
   item `failed`, issue `blocked`, BLOCKER to the human with the findings and the `asf merge retry`
   hint.
4. `max_rounds` handling in `enter_review` is unchanged: once it is reached the human decides.
5. The worker brief's finish ritual mentions that a reviewer may send it back with a
   `review-<round>.md` file and that it then finishes again the same way.

## Out of scope

- No change to how verdicts are parsed or to the reviewer brief.
- No automatic resume of a closed Claude session (`claude --resume`); an unreachable worker is the
  BLOCKER case.

## Hints

- TDD with the fake runtime in `crates/asf/tests/cli_merge.rs`: verdict `changes` with a reachable
  worker (file written, prompt recorded, no BLOCKER, issue `in-progress`, finish + tick re-queues
  the same item and starts round 2); verdict `changes` with an unreachable worker (today's BLOCKER);
  `max_rounds` reached (unchanged).
- Read the runtime port before assuming how "reachable" can be asked; do not infer Herdr JSON
  fields from memory (`herdr agent --help`, project CLAUDE.md "Docs/types first").
- If you need a file outside your scope, ask with a `SCOPE:` QUESTION as the brief describes.

acceptance.text: A changes verdict with a reachable idle worker writes review-<round>.md into the worktree, prompts the worker with one line, posts STATUS instead of a BLOCKER and puts the issue back to in-progress
After the worker finishes again and verification passes, the same merge item is queued again and the next review round starts without an operator command
With an unreachable worker the item is failed, the issue blocked and the human gets the BLOCKER with the findings, as today
max_rounds still stops further reviewers and asks the human
cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test --workspace pass

title: Gates: a linker-lock rerun that makes progress does not use up an attempt
body:
## Problem

asf-51 gave the gate runner a longer pause schedule for a linker lock (`LNK1104`) when there is
nothing to move aside, but the number of attempts is still fixed at 5. On 2026-11-06 the `test`
gate of asf-29 still failed after all 5 attempts (15 + 30 + 60 + 60 s of waiting).

The operator then rebuilt the tests of two freshly rebased worktrees by hand
(`cargo test --workspace --no-run`, rerun every 20 s) and saw the pattern:

```
asf-31: attempt 1 hit LNK1104 on 1 file(s)
asf-31: attempt 2 hit LNK1104 on 4 file(s)
asf-31: attempt 3 hit LNK1104 on 3 file(s)
asf-31: warm build OK on attempt 4
```

Each attempt links more executables and then trips over DIFFERENT files: the antivirus (McAfee
real-time scanning on this machine; folders cannot be excluded) holds whatever was created last.
After a rebase the whole workspace relinks 30+ test executables, so 5 attempts are sometimes not
enough even though every attempt makes progress.

## Wanted behaviour

1. A rerun caused by `LNK1104` does not count against the attempt limit as long as the attempt made
   progress, i.e. the set of files named on `LNK1104` lines differs from the set of the previous
   attempt. Attempts that fail on the same set of files keep counting, with the limit of 5 as today.
2. A hard cap on the total number of reruns (suggested: 12) and the gate's own `timeout_s` per
   attempt still apply, so a gate can never loop forever.
3. The note in the gate tail says which case happened, in plain words (for example
   `linker lock on 3 other file(s); progress, rerun 6 (does not count)`).
4. Pause lengths stay injectable so tests do not sleep; no new config key.
5. Behaviour without `LNK1104` in the output is unchanged (no rerun).

## Out of scope

- No change to `GateResult` fields or to how the merge queue reacts to a failed gate.
- No attempt to detect or configure the antivirus.

## Hints

- TDD in `crates/asf-vcs/tests/gates.rs`, in the style asf-51 used (a fake gate command in Python
  that prints `LNK1104` lines naming different missing paths on successive calls, counted in a temp
  file).
- If `cargo test` itself hits `LNK1104` while you work, rerun it: that is the problem this issue is
  about and not a defect in your change.

acceptance.text: An LNK1104 rerun whose locked-file set differs from the previous attempt does not count against the limit of 5; reruns on the same set still do
A hard cap on the total number of reruns stops the gate even when every attempt reports different files
The gate tail says in plain words whether a rerun counted and why
Failures without LNK1104 are not rerun; pause lengths stay injectable and no config key is added
cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test --workspace pass

title: Serve: a long gate run must not block the tick
body:
## Problem

`asf serve` runs everything inside one tick, one step after another: verification of finished runs
(all gates), the merge queue (rebase, all gates, `verify_main_after`), promotion, dispatch. A full
gate run takes 10 to 40 minutes on this machine. While it runs the loop does nothing else:

- a reviewer's verdict that arrived is not read, so the reviewer's slot stays taken;
- ready issues are not started although worker slots are free;
- a worker that asks a question or stalls is not noticed (no BLOCKER, no notification);
- `--interval 30 --max-ticks 80` took about 3.5 hours on 2026-11-06 instead of 40 minutes, and the
  JSON line of a tick is written only when the tick ends, so the log is silent for that long.

## Wanted behaviour

1. A long gate run (run verification, merge-queue gates, `verify_main_after`) must not stop the
   loop from doing its cheap steps. While a gate run is in flight, the following ticks still watch
   runs (blocked, stalled, questions), read review verdicts, promote and dispatch, and each tick
   still ends within a few seconds.
2. At most ONE gate run is in flight at a time (they are heavy and fight over the linker and the
   antivirus). The merge queue stays strictly FIFO: no item overtakes the one being gated.
3. The state survives a restart: when `asf serve` is stopped while a gate run is in flight, the
   next start neither loses the item nor leaves it in `gating` forever; it reruns the gate.
4. `asf merge tick --once` and `asf serve --once` keep their meaning for scripts and tests: they
   return when the step they started is finished (blocking is fine there), or the report says
   clearly that a gate run is still in flight. State which one you chose in a DECISION comment.
5. The tick report (`--json`) shows a gate run in flight (issue id, gate name, seconds running).

## Design freedom and limits

How the gate run leaves the tick is your choice: a child process (`asf` re-invoking itself for one
gate run, result written to the store), or a thread owned by `serve`. Whatever you choose:

- the store stays the single source of truth (no state only in memory that a restart would lose);
- SQLite writes stay short IMMEDIATE transactions; no transaction is held across a gate run;
- before writing code, post a DECISION comment with the design in five to ten lines.

## Out of scope

- No parallel gate runs, no change to gate definitions or to `GateResult`.
- No change to the TUI.

## Hints

- Read `crates/asf/src/commands/serve.rs`, `merge.rs` (`process`, `tick`) and `run.rs` (watch,
  verify) first; tests with the fake runtime live in `crates/asf/tests/cli_serve.rs`,
  `cli_merge.rs`, `cli_run.rs`.
- A slow fake gate for tests: a Python one-liner that sleeps, as in `crates/asf-vcs/tests/gates.rs`.
- If you need a file outside your scope, ask with a `SCOPE:` QUESTION as the brief describes.

acceptance.text: While a gate run is in flight, following serve ticks still read review verdicts, notice blocked or asking workers, promote and dispatch, and each tick ends within a few seconds
At most one gate run is in flight and the merge queue stays FIFO; an approved item that only needs re-gating after main moved keeps its place in the queue (it is not sent to the back)

Dispatch of ready issues happens in every tick before or independently of the merge-queue step, so a queue of several items never delays worker starts (2026-11-08: the first tick after a restart processed four queue items for an hour before starting any worker)
Stopping asf serve during a gate run loses nothing: the next start reruns the gate and the item does not stay in gating
The tick JSON report shows the gate run in flight with issue id, gate name and seconds running
A DECISION comment describes the chosen design and what --once does
cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test --workspace pass

title: Config: say truthfully when a changed key takes effect (no stale 'restart asf serve' hint)

title: Serve: remind the human when something waits too long (runtime notification + own command)
body:
## Problem

When something needs the human (an issue goes `blocked`, a merge item fails, a worker asks a
question, a run stalls or runs over budget), asf posts one BLOCKER comment and at most one runtime
notification. If the human misses it, nothing happens again: on 2026-11-06 asf-27 and asf-46 sat in
`blocked` and the owner only noticed by looking at the board. The owner asked for a more active
signal when something hangs too long, and chose (2026-11-06): repeated runtime notification plus an
optional command of the owner's own, first reminder after 15 minutes, then every 30 minutes, both
configurable.

## Wanted behaviour

1. New config section (documented in the generated config template, defaults as shown):

   ```toml
   [notify]
   remind_after_minutes = 15   # 0 switches reminders off
   remind_every_minutes = 30
   # command = ["pwsh", "-File", "notify.ps1"]   # optional; run once per reminder, no shell
   ```

2. Each `asf serve` tick collects what is waiting for the human, with the time it has been waiting:
   - issues in `blocked`;
   - merge items in `failed` or `blocked`;
   - runs in `blocked` (worker asks), `stalled`, `over_budget`, `failed`;
   - QUESTION comments addressed to `human` that have no ANSWER.
   One waiting thing per issue is enough (pick the oldest); do not remind twice for the same issue
   because both its run and its merge item are in a bad state.
3. A thing waiting for at least `remind_after_minutes` gets a reminder; it is repeated every
   `remind_every_minutes` while it is still waiting, and stops as soon as it is no longer waiting.
   When it was last reminded is kept in the store (an event such as `attention.reminded` with issue
   id, kind and age), so a restart of `asf serve` neither forgets nor repeats a reminder early.
4. A reminder does two things:
   - a runtime notification through the existing runtime port (title with the issue id, one plain
     sentence such as `asf-27 has been blocked for 45 min: gate test timed out`);
   - when `command` is set: runs it without a shell, with the environment variables

- No TUI change (a separate issue marks overdue rows in the Now view).

- The texts are for a human in a hurry: say what waits, for how long, and the reason in a few

  decides which reminders are due; keep that function free of IO and test it directly.
- Read the runtime port for the notification call before assuming its name or arguments.

title: Start: a start timeout with the agent already up must not fail the reviewer or leave the prompt unsent
body:
Observed again on 2026-11-06 19:5x (reviewer asf-72 for asf-32; earlier asf-36, and workers asf-8, asf-12, asf-20, asf-21): the start of a Claude session ends with 'timeout: timed out waiting for agent status (timeout)'. The run goes to `blocked`, and for a reviewer `enter_review` marks the merge item `failed` ('cannot start the reviewer: worker for asf-72 is blocked at startup'). `asf serve --until-done` then stops with 'stuck'.

What the runtime showed right after: `herdr agent list` reports the agent as `idle` with `interactive_ready: true`, and the pane shows the kick-off line ('Start asf-72: read .factory/runs/asf-72/brief.md and follow it.') typed into the input box but NOT submitted; cost 0.00, tool calls 0. So Claude did start; the runtime reported it late and the prompt was never sent. The retry added by asf-25 did not rescue this case.

Wanted:
1. Find out first, from the code and from the runtime's own help, why the prompt ends up typed but unsent and which step timed out (docs/types first: `herdr agent --help`; do not infer flags or JSON fields from memory). State the cause in the report.
2. When the start wait times out, read the agent state once more. If the agent is up and ready, continue the start (send or re-send the kick-off prompt, confirm it was accepted) instead of marking the run `blocked`.
3. If the agent is really not up after the existing retry, behave as today for a worker (run `blocked`, BLOCKER). For a reviewer, do not burn the merge item: close the failed reviewer run and its review issue, leave the item where the next tick starts a fresh reviewer, and give up with `failed` only after 2 failed reviewer starts in a row.
4. A kick-off prompt must never stay typed and unsent: after sending, verify that the agent left the idle state or that the input is empty, and resend the submit key if not.

Out of scope: no change to verdict handling or to the gates.

A start whose wait times out while the agent is up and ready continues: the kick-off prompt is sent and confirmed, the run becomes working

A reviewer that cannot be started does not fail the merge item on the first try: its run and review issue are closed and the next tick starts a fresh reviewer; after 2 failed starts in a row the item fails with a BLOCKER
After the kick-off the start code verifies that the prompt was submitted and presses the submit key again if it was not

title: Serve: notify the human at once when a worker asks or something blocks (not only when things go well)
body:
Observed 2026-11-07: worker asf-68 posted a SCOPE QUESTION to human (#190) and later a BLOCKER (#199). The owner never saw either until he asked the operator. Reading the code: asf sends a runtime notification in exactly two places, both good news: 'asf <id> merged' (commands/merge.rs, finalize_merged) and 'asf <id> verified' (worker.rs, after verification). Nothing is sent when a QUESTION or BLOCKER addressed to human is posted, when a run goes blocked (worker dialog), stalled, over_budget or failed, or when a merge item fails or is blocked. The 'claude needs attention' toast the owner sometimes sees comes from Herdr itself on agent status changes and carries no issue id or text. asf-68 adds reminders after [notify] after_minutes (15 min) for things that keep waiting, but there is no notification at the moment the wait starts.

Wanted:
1. The serve loop notifies the human immediately, once, when something new starts waiting for them: a QUESTION or BLOCKER comment addressed to human, a run entering blocked / stalled / over_budget / failed, a merge item entering failed or blocked, an issue entering blocked. 'New' means since the previous tick; use the store (events or comment ids), not memory, so a restart does not re-notify or miss things.
2. Reuse what asf-68 built: the same collection of 'what waits for the human', the same runtime notification call, the same optional [notify] command with the same environment variables (ASF_REMIND_KIND may then be, for example, 'question', 'blocker', 'run_blocked', 'merge_failed'), and record the notification in the store the way asf-68 records a reminder, so the first reminder is counted from the notification time.
3. The text is for a human in a hurry: title 'asf <id> asks' / 'asf <id> is blocked' / 'asf <id> merge failed', body = first line of the question, blocker or last_error, cut to one line. Sound: the runtime's attention sound, not the 'done' one.
4. The two existing good-news notifications stay as they are.
5. [notify] after_minutes = 0 (reminders off) does not switch the immediate notification off; add one boolean [notify] on_new = true for that, editable with asf config set.

Out of scope: no TUI change; no new external channels (the command is the extension point).

acceptance.text: A new QUESTION or BLOCKER to human, a run entering blocked, stalled, over_budget or failed, a merge item entering failed or blocked, or an issue entering blocked produces exactly one runtime notification in the next serve tick, with the issue id and the first line of the text, and runs the [notify] command when set
A restart of asf serve neither repeats nor loses these notifications; the first reminder of asf-68 is counted from the notification
[notify] on_new defaults to true, is editable with asf config set, and false switches only the immediate notifications off
The existing merged and verified notifications are unchanged

title: Issue: an ANSWER to a worker without --reply-to should still resolve its open QUESTION
body:
Observed 2026-11-07: the operator answered worker asf-68's SCOPE question with `asf issue comment asf-68 --type ANSWER --to asf-68 --body ...` but without `--reply-to 190`. `unanswered_questions` (crates/asf/src/commands/issue.rs) counts a QUESTION as answered only when an ANSWER has `reply_to == question.id`, so `asf issue finish` would still have refused, although the human had answered on the issue. The operator noticed by luck.

Wanted:
1. `asf issue comment --type ANSWER` without `--reply-to` links the answer to the newest unanswered QUESTION of the addressed lane on that issue (`--to <lane>`), and says so in its output (`answers #190`). With several open questions and no `--reply-to`, it refuses with exit 2 and lists them, so nothing is linked by accident.
2. An ANSWER that resolves a question sets the question's `resolved_at` (today it stays null even with `--reply-to`), so the inbox and the Now view stop showing it.
3. `asf issue finish` keeps the guard as is; the TUI answer path (`a`) is out of scope unless it already calls the same command.
Tests in crates/asf/tests/cli_issue.rs: answer without reply-to resolves the only open question and finish then passes; two open questions and no reply-to refuse with exit 2; an answer with reply-to sets resolved_at.

acceptance.text: An ANSWER without --reply-to is linked to the single open QUESTION of the addressed lane and finish then passes; with several open questions it refuses with exit 2 and lists them
An ANSWER that resolves a QUESTION sets its resolved_at, and the inbox no longer shows it

body:
Observed 2026-11-07 19:42 on asf-79 (first live use of asf-64 send_back): the merge queue had rebased feat/asf-79 onto main (aa6f787) before the review; the reviewer asked for changes; merge::send_back reopened the run; the worker fixed and ran `asf issue finish`; verification then failed with 'files outside scope' listing EVERY file main had changed since the run started (README.md, crates/asf-vcs/src/gates.rs, the whole tui/ tree ...). Cause: the run row still carries the base_sha from the original start (8bacbe9), while the branch now sits on aa6f787, so changed_files(base_sha) includes main's own commits. The same will hit asf-65 (base c04884d, branch rebased onto e8cc964). Operator workaround: UPDATE runs SET base_sha = <git merge-base main feat/<id>> and `asf run verify <id>`.

Wanted:
1. Verification (worker.rs verify path and `asf run verify`) computes the diff against the merge-base of the branch and the default branch (git merge-base), never against a stored base_sha that may predate a rebase. Keep base_sha in the run row for information only, or refresh it whenever the queue rebases the branch (both are fine; say which in a DECISION).
2. send_back (asf-64) and the merge queue's rebase step keep the run's base_sha in sync with the rebased branch, so other readers of base_sha (reports, reviewer brief 'base_sha in the brief predates the rebase' remarks seen today) stop being misleading.
3. Tests: a flow test in crates/asf/tests/cli_merge.rs or cli_run.rs: start, finish, verify, enqueue, rebase onto a moved main, review verdict changes, worker finishes again -> verification passes and reports only the worker's files.

Out of scope: no change to the scope rules themselves.

acceptance.text: After the queue rebases a branch and a changes verdict reopens its run, the worker's second finish verifies against the rebased base and lists only the worker's files
base_sha stored on the run is refreshed by the rebase or ignored by verification, as stated in a DECISION comment
