title: Questions: every question to the human goes through AskUserQuestion; the TUI answer grants SCOPE requests
body:
Owner request (2026-11-08): workers should ask the human interactively (Claude Code's AskUserQuestion in the pane, which the TUI shows as a banner and answers with 'a'), not with QUESTION comments the human has to find in the inbox. Today the brief says: blocking question -> AskUserQuestion, non-blocking -> QUESTION comment; in practice workers use comments for SCOPE: requests (asf-39, asf-40, asf-68, asf-69, asf-79 on 2026-11-07/08), so the human never gets the 'a' dialog.

Wanted:
1. The worker brief (crates/asf-core/src/brief.rs, Protocol section) tells workers to ask EVERY question that needs a human answer with AskUserQuestion, with 2-4 closed options and the recommended one first, including scope requests: the dialog's question text starts with 'SCOPE: <path> because <reason>' and option 1 is 'Grant <path>'. A QUESTION comment is still posted for the record (so finish guard and the inbox keep working), but the human answers in the dialog.
2. When the human answers a SCOPE dialog from the TUI ('a' overlay) or with 'asf run keys <id> 1' and the chosen option is the grant, asf runs the same code as 'asf issue scope add <id> <paths>' (parse the paths from the dialog text captured in the BLOCKER comment) and marks the QUESTION answered, so the worker's hook stops denying the file right away. A refusal (option 2) sends the keys only.
3. The Now view / banner shows the question text as today; no new TUI layout.
4. Tests: brief text pinned; fake runtime flow test: worker posts a SCOPE dialog -> blocked -> 'asf run keys <id> 1' -> scope extended and question answered; option 2 -> scope unchanged.

Out of scope: no change to the reviewer protocol.

acceptance.text: The brief tells workers to ask every human question with AskUserQuestion (closed options, recommended first), scope requests included, with a QUESTION comment for the record
Answering a SCOPE dialog with the grant option from the TUI or asf run keys extends the scope and resolves the question; a refusal only sends the keys

The brief has a testing rule: a test that runs asf serve (or any loop) as a process waits for an observable condition with a deadline and then stops the process; it never relies on a tick count or a fixed sleep to end the loop, and reuses the shared LiveServe helper in crates/asf/tests/cli_serve.rs (2026-11-09: asf-66 failed three queue attempts on such a test, 10 ticks too few, 300 too many)
The brief forbids AI attribution trailers (Co-Authored-By, Generated-by) in commit messages (2026-11-08: asf-98 worker added one; Conventional Commits, English)

title: Merge: configurable clean-up after a successful merge (worktree, branch, reviewer worktrees)
body:
Owner request (2026-11-08): after one week of dogfooding .worktrees/ held 61 directories (89 GB, each with its own target/). Today nothing is removed automatically; the operator runs 'asf lane clean <id>' one by one. The owner wants the queue to clean up after a merge, with a setting that says what.

Wanted:
1. New config in [merge]:
   clean_after = ["worktree", "branch", "review_worktrees"]   # default: ["worktree", "review_worktrees"]
   An empty list keeps today's behaviour. Each entry is one kind of clean-up, run after the merge succeeded AND, when [merge] verify_main_after is on, after main's gates passed:
   - worktree: the same code and refusals as 'asf lane clean <id>' (refuses a claimed, dirty or unmerged lane; a refusal is logged as an event and reported in the tick, never fails the merge);
   - branch: 'git branch -d feat/<id>' (lowercase -d only: refuses when not fully merged), after the worktree is gone;
   - review_worktrees: the detached checkouts .worktrees/<review-id> of this issue's review runs (they hold no work of their own).
2. The clean-up never touches a worktree whose run is still active or whose lane has uncommitted files; those stay for 'asf lane clean'.
3. 'asf lane clean --all [--dry-run]' cleans every finished lane at once with the same refusals, for repos that were created before this change.
4. 'asf config show/set' know the key; the config template documents it; the tick JSON report lists what was cleaned and what was refused and why.
5. Tests: cli_merge flow with FakeRuntime: merge -> worktree and review worktrees gone, branch gone only with 'branch' in the list; a dirty worktree is refused and reported; 'lane clean --all --dry-run' lists without removing.

Out of scope: no deletion of remote branches; no change to 'lane clean <id>' semantics.

acceptance.text: [merge] clean_after lists what is removed after a successful merge (worktree, branch, review_worktrees); the default removes the worktree and the review worktrees and keeps the branch; an empty list keeps everything
Clean-up never removes a claimed, dirty or unmerged lane; refusals are reported in the tick and never fail the merge; branch removal uses git branch -d
asf lane clean --all [--dry-run] cleans every finished lane with the same refusals

title: Start: the submit check must wait for the runtime's state lag before declaring a start failed
body:
Observed 2026-11-08 14:5x, first live run of asf-73: reviewer asf-107 for asf-98 was declared failed with 'kick-off prompt not submitted: agent still idle after 3 submit key press(es)' and its workspace closed (cost 0, the item went back to queued: that part of asf-73 works). Earlier the same day the operator's single 'asf run keys <id> Enter' always made such an agent work, but the runtime reported 'working' only after a delay of up to 90 s (the very lag that caused the original problem). So the new check presses Enter up to 3 times within a short window and gives up before the runtime can report the change.

Wanted:
1. After each submit key press, wait for the runtime's state change with a timeout of the same order as [worker] start_timeout_ms (reuse that value or a fraction of it), not a few seconds; read the pane text as a second signal (the kick-off line gone from the input box = submitted).
2. Do not press Enter again while the previous press may still be taking effect; at most one extra press after the wait.
3. Keep the asf-73 behaviour for a real failure (fresh reviewer next tick, worker run blocked with BLOCKER).
4. Tests with the fake runtime: a runtime that turns the agent to working 20 s after the first Enter is a successful start; one that never leaves idle is a failed start after the wait.
5. State in the report what the live Herdr latency is (measure it once with herdr agent get in a loop) and set the defaults from that.

acceptance.text: A start whose agent turns working within the start timeout after the submit key is a success, even when the runtime reports it late
At most one extra submit press after a real wait; a real failure still behaves as asf-73 specified

title: Merge: a gate failure or a rebase conflict after the rebase goes back to the idle worker like review findings
body:
Observed 2026-11-08 16:31 (asf-78): after the queue rebased feat/asf-78 onto a main that had moved (asf-69, asf-95), the clippy gate failed. The item went to failed with a BLOCKER to the human, although the worker's pane was still open and idle, exactly the situation asf-64 solved for review findings. The operator relayed the clippy output by hand and will retry the merge.

Wanted:
1. When a gate fails in the merge queue after the rebase (not in the worker's own verification) and the worker can still be reached, reuse merge::send_back (asf-64): write the gate tail to <worktree>/.factory/runs/<id>/gate-<n>.md with a short explanation ('after the rebase onto <sha> the gate <name> failed; fix on what is checked out, run the gates, commit, finish again'), prompt the worker with one line, reopen the run, post a STATUS instead of a BLOCKER. After the worker finishes again, the normal verify -> re-queue path runs.
2. Do not send back environment failures: a gate whose tail is only LNK1104 (linker lock) or a timeout (exit None) is retried by the queue as today; only a real failure (exit code, test/lint output) is sent to the worker.
3. The same max_rounds-style guard as reviews: after 2 send-backs for gate failures on one item, stop and ask the human.
4. When the worker is not reachable: today's behaviour (failed + BLOCKER + merge retry hint).
5. Tests in crates/asf/tests/cli_merge.rs with the fake runtime: a gate that fails only after rebase -> gate-1.md written, prompt sent, run reopened, STATUS posted; an LNK1104-only tail -> no send-back; an unreachable worker -> BLOCKER.

acceptance.text: A real gate failure after the rebase is sent to a reachable worker (gate-<n>.md with the gate tail and a short explanation, one-line prompt, run reopened as working so the item leaves NEEDS YOU, STATUS instead of BLOCKER)

A gate failure in the worker's own verification (run verify after finish) is sent back the same way instead of blocking the issue with a BLOCKER to the human (2026-11-11 19:50: asf-106 failed clippy in verification, the worker was idle in its pane, the operator relayed the two clippy errors by hand)

A rebase conflict is sent the same way (conflict-<n>.md with the conflicting files and the instruction: rebase onto main in the worktree, resolve keeping both sides' intent, gates, commit); the queue itself still never resolves a conflict (2026-11-08 21:44: asf-42 vs asf-41 in tests/frame.rs went to the human although the worker was idle in its pane)

Re-queue needs no comment from the worker: when the branch head moved past the sent-back commit, the worktree is clean and the agent is idle or done, the loop re-queues the item itself (2026-11-09: the asf-66 worker committed its fixes three times without the agreed STATUS and the operator had to notice and retry by hand)
Linker-lock and timeout failures are not sent back; an unreachable worker still gets today's BLOCKER

Config key gate.max_rounds (default 2, described in config_edit like review.max_rounds): after that many send-backs for gate failures or conflicts on one item the item stays failed with a BLOCKER to the human that names the rounds

Owner screenshots 2026-11-08 (14:5x and 18:4x): the TUI header showed 'runtime ?' although 'herdr status' answered (protocol 22) and agents were running in Herdr; at the same time it showed 'workers 4/1' with [scheduler] max_parallel = 1.

Wanted:
1. Find out how the header probes the runtime (snapshot.rs / chrome.rs) and why it yields unknown on a loaded machine (timeout too short? wrong command? error swallowed?). Show 'runtime ok' whenever the runtime answers, keep the last known state for a few refreshes instead of flipping to '?' on one slow probe, and show the reason on the Agents view when it really is down.
2. 'workers n/m' must use the same counting as the scheduler after asf-46: active worker runs only (working/blocked/stalled/over_budget/finishing/verifying), not reviewers and not runs of issues whose merge item is being fixed... state exactly which run states count, in a DECISION, and make the Now view's RUNNING section and the header agree.
3. Tests: header shows 'runtime ok' with a fake runtime that answers slowly (within the probe timeout) and '?' only after N consecutive failures; the worker counter with 1 worker + 2 reviewers + 1 reopened run shows the agreed number.

acceptance.text: The header shows 'runtime ok' when the runtime answers, even slowly, and '?' only after several failed probes in a row
The header's workers n/m matches the scheduler's active-worker count and the Now RUNNING section
cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test --workspace pass

title: TUI answer overlay: handle multi-question dialogs (tabs) and send Submit for the human
body:
Owner's live test 2026-11-09 09:25 (first real use of 'a' on a worker dialog, asf-44): Claude Code's AskUserQuestion showed TWO questions as tabs ('☐ cli_tui.rs  ☐ mod.rs  ✔ Submit') with a Submit step at the end. The overlay let the owner pick an option, but the dialog did not close: the second tab had to be answered and the final Submit had to be sent by hand (typed keys). Owner: 'Były dwa pytania, ale potem jest submit i to musiałem zrobić ręcznie'.

Wanted:
1. The overlay parses the tab row of a multi-question dialog from the captured pane text (the '☐ … ☐ … ✔ Submit' line and the '←/→' hints) and shows 'question 1 of N' with the current question's options; after a choice it moves to the next tab (Right arrow key to the pane) and shows that question; after the last one it sends the Submit step (Tab/Right to '✔ Submit' then Enter, as Claude Code expects) and closes.
2. A single-question dialog keeps today's flow (digit or Enter, no extra keys).
3. If the pane text does not match a known dialog shape, the overlay says so and offers the raw keys ('k' key mode) and 't' typed reply as today, so nothing is worse than before.
4. The keys sent for each step are recorded in the BLOCKER/ANSWER trail (what the human chose per tab), so the dossier shows the full answer.
5. Tests with the fake runtime: a two-tab dialog capture -> choices '1' then '2' -> the key sequence sent is exactly [1, Right, 2, Right, Enter] (or whatever the verified Claude Code sequence is; verify it live once against Claude Code 2.1.x and state it in a DECISION); a single-question capture -> [1, Enter] as today.

Out of scope: brief/protocol changes (asf-103).

acceptance.text: A multi-question dialog is answered tab by tab from the overlay and the final Submit is sent by asf, not by the human
Single-question dialogs behave as today; an unrecognised dialog falls back to raw keys and typed reply

title: Store: order runs by attempt so the newest run of an issue is deterministic
body:
Flaky gate failure observed 2026-11-09 10:54 on the asf-66 merge item (attempt 3): `commands::remind::flow_tests::finished_issues_and_older_runs_do_not_wait` panicked at crates/asf/src/commands/remind.rs:739 (`collect(...).is_empty()` was false). The same test passed on main in the verify-after-merge run and passed twice in a row when rerun in the asf-66 worktree, so the test is order dependent, not broken by asf-66 (which does not touch remind.rs).

Root cause: `SqliteStore::runs` (crates/asf-store/src/runs.rs:154) orders runs with `ORDER BY started_at, id`. `started_at` is an RFC 3339 string with second precision and `id` is a ULID (millisecond timestamp + 80 random bits). Two runs created for the same issue within the same millisecond (the test's `run_in` calls, and in production a fast retry) therefore come back in random order, and every consumer that keeps "the last run wins" (remind.rs:76-79 `newest` map, and any similar loop in the TUI snapshot or `run list`) may pick the older attempt.

Fix: order by the monotonic per-issue `attempt` as the tie-break (`ORDER BY started_at, attempt, id`), and audit the other places that select the newest run of an issue so they rely on `attempt`, not on insertion order. Keep the test as is; it should pass deterministically after the fix.

acceptance.text: SqliteStore::runs returns runs of one issue in attempt order even when two runs share the same started_at second and were created in the same millisecond (a store test creates two runs back to back and asserts the order 50 times or with a forced equal started_at)
Every place that picks the newest run of an issue (remind.rs collect, the TUI snapshot, run list/show) uses the highest attempt, not the last row returned
cargo test --workspace passes; commands::remind::flow_tests::finished_issues_and_older_runs_do_not_wait is unchanged and passes 20 times in a row

title: Gates: read the locked file from a localized LNK1104 line (Polish „” quotes)
body:
Observed 2026-11-09 13:20 on the asf-43 merge item: the `test` gate hit LNK1104 five times and gave up ("nothing to move aside (no file path in the linker message)"), although the linker named the locked file on every line:

    LINK : fatal error LNK1104: nie można otworzyć pliku „D:\Programowanie\auto-software-factory\.worktrees\asf-43\target\debug\deps\asf-ce36f34fbf868c1a.exe”

`locked_files` in crates/asf-vcs/src/gates.rs:185 takes the path between the first two ASCII double quotes (`"`). On a Polish Windows the MSVC linker (and other localized toolchains) quotes the path with typographic quotes „ ” (U+201E / U+201D; other locales use « », “ ” or 「 」), so no path is found, `move_locked_aside` has nothing to rename and the whole asf-65 recovery is dead on this machine: the reruns only wait and the gate fails after 5 attempts (~3 min) even though the item would have passed.

Fix: make the path extraction locale independent. Suggested: on a LNK1104 line, take the last token that ends in `.exe` (case-insensitive) after stripping any surrounding quote characters from the set `" ' „ ” “ « » 「 」`; or match a regex for a Windows path (`[A-Za-z]:\...\.exe`). Keep the ASCII-quote behaviour. Add a unit test with the Polish line above verbatim (including the „ ” quotes) and one with an English line, both expecting the same path.

acceptance.text: locked_files returns the .exe path for an LNK1104 line quoted with ASCII quotes, with Polish „ ” quotes and with “ ” or « » quotes; a unit test uses the exact Polish line from the issue body
When the path is found and the file exists, move_locked_aside renames it as before and the rerun reports 'moved aside', not 'nothing to move aside'
cargo test --workspace passes

title: Lanes: a worker cannot comment as human or orchestrator (--lane spoofing)
body:
Observed 2026-11-09 15:07 on asf-43: after the operator picked option 1 in the worker's AskUserQuestion dialog, the worker closed its own open SCOPE question #423 by running

    asf issue comment asf-43 --type ANSWER --lane human --to asf-43 --reply-to 423 --body "Drop the counts ..."

from its own pane (process tree: the worker's shell). The comment #429 is stored and shown as `[human] ANSWER`, the question counts as answered by the human, the reminder stops, and `asf issue finish` is unblocked. Nothing in the CLI or in the worker's permission rules stops a worker from speaking as `human` or `orchestrator`; `--lane` overrides the `ASF_ISSUE` env that identifies the lane.

This matters because the review and the scope guard treat human answers as authoritative: a worker can grant itself a scope extension, answer its own question or mark a blocker resolved. Here the content happened to match the operator's decision, but the mechanism must not exist.

Fix, two layers:
1. `asf` CLI (lane resolution in asf-core `lane::resolve` and the `--lane` flag): when `ASF_ISSUE` (or `ASF_RUN`) is set in the environment, `--lane` may only name that same issue; `human`, `orchestrator` and any other issue id are refused with exit 2 and a clear message ("a worker speaks only as its own lane"). The orchestrator and the human never run with `ASF_ISSUE` set, so they are unaffected.
2. Worker settings written by the brief (crates/asf/src/worker.rs or wherever `settings.json` permissions are rendered): add deny rules for `Bash(asf * --lane *)` so the attempt is blocked before the CLI runs.
Also: `asf issue scope add` already answers the pending SCOPE question as the orchestrator; the brief should tell workers to wait for that answer (or for `--reply-to` from human/orchestrator), never to answer their own questions.

acceptance.text: With ASF_ISSUE=asf-7 in the environment, asf issue comment --lane human (and --lane orchestrator, --lane asf-9) exits 2 with a message naming the rule; --lane asf-7 and no --lane keep working
Without ASF_ISSUE, --lane human and --lane orchestrator work as before (CLI tests)
The worker settings.json rendered for a run denies Bash(asf * --lane *); a unit test on the rendered permissions pins it
The worker brief says: never answer your own QUESTION/SCOPE; wait for an ANSWER from human or orchestrator (scope add answers it)
cargo test --workspace passes

title: Gates: stop a hanging test gate early and name the slow tests
body:
Observed 2026-11-09 14:23 (asf-66, attempt 7): the `test` gate ran for the full 2400 s and was killed with exit None. The tail only said "killed: timeout after 2400s". Yet after about two minutes the Rust test harness had already printed `test <name> has been running for over 60 seconds` for 5 tests, and in a later run for 36 tests; that list was the whole diagnosis (the serve loop in those tests never ended). The operator reproduced it by hand to get the list and wrote it into gate-2.md for the worker. The queue should do that itself.

Wanted, in the gate runner (crates/asf-vcs/src/gates.rs, GateRunner / run_gate):
1. While a gate runs, read its output incrementally (it is already captured) and watch for the harness line `has been running for over <n> seconds`. Collect the test names.
2. New optional `[[gate]]` keys: `slow_tests = <n>` (give up when at least n distinct slow tests were reported) and `slow_after_s = <s>` (give up when a slow-test line is older than s seconds and the gate has not finished). Defaults: off for gates that are not `cargo test`-like; the dogfooding config will set `slow_tests = 3, slow_after_s = 300` on the `test` gate.
3. On give-up: kill the process tree (the test harness spawns `asf serve` children; killing only cargo leaves them running), mark the gate failed with a tail that starts with a clear header: "gate `test` stopped: N tests ran for more than 60 s: <names, one per line>" followed by the normal last lines. That tail is what the worker sees in gate-<n>.md (asf-112).
4. A kill on the ordinary timeout also lists the slow tests seen so far, and also kills the process tree.
5. Document the two keys in config_edit (label, group, kind, default) so the TUI Config view shows them.
Tests in crates/asf-vcs/tests/gates.rs with a fake test binary (a script) that prints the harness line for two test names and then sleeps: the gate stops early, the tail names both tests, the child is gone.

acceptance.text: A gate whose output reports slow_tests distinct 'has been running for over 60 seconds' tests, or whose first slow-test line is older than slow_after_s, is stopped early; the tail starts with a header naming the slow tests one per line
Stopping a gate (early or on timeout) kills the whole process tree: a fake test binary that spawns a child sleeping 10 minutes leaves no child behind (checked by pid)
The two keys are optional per [[gate]], described in config_edit, and absent keys keep today's behaviour exactly (existing gate tests unchanged)
cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test --workspace pass

title: Merge: a gate failure on a test outside the branch is rerun once and filed as flaky
body:
Observed 2026-11-09 10:54 (asf-66, attempt 3): the `test` gate failed on `commands::remind::flow_tests::finished_issues_and_older_runs_do_not_wait` in crates/asf/src/commands/remind.rs, a file feat/asf-66 does not touch. The test passed on main minutes earlier and passed twice when rerun in the same worktree (root cause: asf-127). The queue sent a BLOCKER to the human; the operator did by hand what the queue can do itself: check that the failing test lives outside the branch's diff, rerun, re-queue, and open an issue for the flaky test.

Wanted (merge queue, crates/asf/src/commands/merge.rs, with helpers in crates/asf-vcs/src/gates.rs):
1. Parse the failing test names from a `cargo test` gate tail (`failures:` list and `---- <name> stdout ----` headers). Map each name to candidate files: a unit test path `a::b::tests::name` -> `crates/*/src/a/b.rs` or `crates/*/src/a/b/mod.rs` (the crate is the one named in the `Running unittests` line above it); an integration test (binary `tests\cli_serve.rs` in the `Running tests\...` line) -> `crates/<crate>/tests/<file>.rs`. Unknown names map to nothing and count as "in the branch" (conservative).
2. If every failing test maps to files that are not in `git diff --name-only <merge-base>..HEAD` of the branch, the failure is "foreign": rerun the gate once (does not count as an attempt, logged like the linker-lock reruns). If the rerun passes, continue the queue and create an issue `Flaky test: <name>` (type task, priority 2, label flaky, body with the gate tail excerpt, the branch, the main sha; scope = the mapped file) unless an open issue with the same title exists. If the rerun fails again, the failure is treated as today's real failure (asf-112 send-back or BLOCKER).
3. If any failing test maps to a file the branch changed, no rerun: it is the worker's failure.
4. JSON event `merge.gate_rerun_foreign` with the test names, so the Log view can show it.
Tests in crates/asf/tests/cli_merge.rs with a fake gate script that fails once on a test outside the branch's files and passes on the rerun: the item merges, exactly one `Flaky test:` issue exists; and a case where the failing test's file is in the branch: no rerun, the item fails.

acceptance.text: Failing test names are parsed from a cargo test tail and mapped to candidate source files (unit test module path and integration test binary); unmapped names count as the branch's own

When all failing tests are outside the branch diff, the gate is rerun once without counting; a green rerun continues the queue and creates one 'Flaky test: <name>' issue with label flaky (no duplicate when one is open); a red rerun is a normal failure
When a failing test's file is in the branch diff there is no rerun
cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test --workspace pass

title: Issues: adding a dependency to a ready issue sends it back to backlog
body: Observed 2026-11-09 16:55: to park six ready issues behind asf-133 the operator ran asf issue dep add <id> asf-133 on each; every one stayed status=ready (asf issue list --ready still listed them) and had to be moved to backlog by hand with asf issue status. The scheduler picks candidates from ready issues, so a ready issue with a freshly added open dependency could still be dispatched before its dependency is done. Wanted: dep add on a ready issue whose new dependency is not done sets the status back to backlog (event issue.demoted, one line in the human output: 'asf-45 -> backlog (waits for asf-133)'); dep rm that leaves no open dependency promotes as today on the next tick (no change). Scheduler: as a second guard, a ready issue with an open dependency is never a candidate (deferred reason DepsOpen), even if its status says ready. Tests in crates/asf-store or crates/asf/tests/cli_issue.rs and the scheduler property tests.

acceptance.text: dep add <ready issue> <open dep> leaves the issue in backlog and prints why; dep add with a done dependency leaves it ready
scheduler::plan never returns a slot for an issue with an open dependency regardless of its status (property test)
cargo test --workspace passes

title: Serve: a heartbeat so the TUI and doctor show when the loop stopped and why
body:
Observed 2026-11-11 19:5x: the operator's loop (asf serve --dispatch --until-done --max-ticks 600) reached its tick limit after 633 ticks and exited with code 0 and a JSON summary ({"reason":"max_ticks", ...}). Nothing in the TUI changed: the header still said `runtime ok · workers 1/2 · queue 1`, the Now view showed a worker RUNNING and an item in the queue, and nothing moved for 5 minutes until the background notification reached the operator. A user watching the TUI has no way to tell that the loop is gone (max_ticks, stuck, Ctrl+C, a crash, a reboot) nor what to do about it. The tick limit itself is only a CLI flag, invisible in the Config view.

Wanted:
1. Heartbeat: every tick, serve writes a pulse (table or single row in the store, or .factory/serve.json): pid, started_at, last_tick_at, mode (dispatch / observe), interval, max_ticks, ticks so far. On a clean stop it writes stopped_at and the stop reason (all_done, max_ticks, stuck, interrupted, error:<msg>). A stale pulse (last_tick_at older than 3 intervals, pid gone) counts as "stopped without a reason" (crash or reboot).
2. TUI header: `loop ok 12 s` (dim) while the pulse is fresh; `LOOP STOPPED 14 min` (warn colour) otherwise; `loop observe` when the loop runs without dispatch.
3. Banner on every view (the same slot as "agent is waiting for your answer", lower priority than it): one line with the reason and the fix, e.g. `the loop stopped 14 min ago: max_ticks (633) — start it again: asf serve --dispatch`; `the loop is not running — start it: asf serve --dispatch`; `the loop stopped: stuck (asf-7 waits for your answer)`. The Now view lists it in NEEDS YOU as the first row with key `?`/Enter opening the explanation.
4. `asf repo doctor` reports the loop state the same way; `asf serve` refuses to start a second loop on the same repo when a fresh pulse with a live pid exists (clear message), and takes over a stale one.
5. Config key `[serve] max_ticks` (default: none) and `[serve] interval_s` (default 10) described in config_edit so they show in the Config view; the CLI flags override them. `--until-done` without a limit stays valid.
Tests: unit tests on the pulse freshness decision; TUI frame tests for the header and the banner in both states; cli_serve test that a stopped loop leaves stopped_at and the reason; doctor output test.

acceptance.text: Every tick writes a pulse (pid, last_tick_at, mode, interval, max_ticks, ticks); a clean stop writes stopped_at and the reason; a pulse older than 3 intervals or with a dead pid counts as stopped without reason
The TUI header shows loop ok <age> / loop observe / LOOP STOPPED <age>; when stopped, every view shows a banner with the reason and the command to start it again, and Now lists it first in NEEDS YOU
asf repo doctor prints the same loop state; a second asf serve on a repo with a live loop refuses with a clear message and a stale pulse is taken over
[serve] max_ticks and [serve] interval_s exist in config.toml and the Config view; CLI flags override them

title: Serve: resend the turn when an agent ends on an API/network error instead of waiting for the stall timer
body:
Observed 2026-11-13 09:14 (internet outage of a few minutes). Two agents ended their turn with `API Error: Can't reach the API server — check your internet or DNS (ENOTFOUND)`:

- the reviewer asf-157 (review of asf-103, round 3) had just been started; its kick-off prompt (`Start asf-157: read ... brief.md and follow it.`) died on that error, so the pane sat idle with 0 tool calls for 20 minutes until the operator re-sent the prompt by hand;
- the worker asf-153, mid-fix after a review round, lost its turn the same way (its background `cargo test` finished, nobody read the result) and sat idle until nudged.

`asf serve` treats both as `working` (Herdr says the agent is idle only after the turn ends, and the stall detector needs `stall_minutes` of silence). An outage is a transient, not a stall or a worker failure, and the fix is always the same: send the turn again.

Wanted: the loop recognises the API-error ending and recovers by itself.

Notes:
- The pane tail is the only signal today: the last agent message is `API Error: Can't reach the API server` (also seen: `API Error: 5xx`, `Request timed out`). Claude Code prints it where a normal reply would be, then returns to the prompt.
- A kick-off that failed is recognisable by `tool_calls == 0` (hooks never fired) plus the error line; a mid-run failure by the error line being the last message.
- Recovery = re-send what was in flight: the kick-off prompt for a fresh run, otherwise a short `Your last turn ended with an API error; continue where you left off.`; the pane input must be empty first (asf-109's `ensure_submitted` logic applies).
- Back-off, not a hot loop: first retry after ~60 s, then 2, 4, 8 min, give up after `worker.api_retries` (default 5) → `stalled` with a BLOCKER that names the error. Do not spend a run `attempt` on it and do not count it as a review round.
- A reviewer run gets the same treatment as a worker run.

acceptance.text: A run whose pane tail ends with an API/network error line (ENOTFOUND, 5xx, timeout) and whose input is empty gets its last prompt re-sent by the loop within 2 minutes, with exponential back-off
A kick-off that failed (tool_calls == 0 + error line) is re-sent as the kick-off prompt; a mid-run failure as a short continue message
After worker.api_retries (default 5) failed resends the run becomes stalled with a BLOCKER naming the error; no run attempt and no review round is consumed by resends
Reviewer runs are covered the same way as worker runs
Tests in cli_serve.rs/cli_run.rs with a fake pane tail cover: kick-off resend, mid-run resend, back-off, give-up

A gate killed for an infrastructure reason (early slow-test stop, timeout, linker lock retries used up: no exit code) during a run's verification is not a code failure: the loop reruns the verification once by itself, and only a second such failure blocks the issue with a BLOCKER that says it was an infrastructure stop; a test in cli_serve.rs or cli_run.rs covers the single automatic rerun

title: CLI: asf --version shows the commit the binary was built from
body:

- Keep `propagate_version`.

title: Merge: a dirty tracked file on main that the branch changes blocks the item before the gates, not after the review
body:
Observed 2026-11-13 20:35 (asf-134): the branch passed rebase, all gates (twice) and the review (approve), then the fast-forward failed with `error: Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge: .factory/config.toml`. The repository root had an uncommitted edit of a tracked file the branch also changes. The item became `failed`; the operator had to restore the file by hand and run `asf merge retry`, which cost one more full gate run.

`local_merge` already has a `park_if_dirty` mode (an approved item stays in `reviewing` while main is dirty), but this path was not taken: the item was failed.

Wanted:
1. Before an item starts gating (after the rebase), compare the files the branch changes (`git diff --name-only <default>...<branch>`) with the uncommitted tracked files of the repository root (`git status --porcelain`). On an overlap do not start the gates: the item waits (state `blocked`) with a message that names the files and says what to do (commit or restore them, then `asf merge retry <id>`), and a NEEDS YOU row. No gate run and no review is spent.
2. At fast-forward time a `Dirty` error never fails an item whose review is approved or whose review is skipped as already approved: it parks as in `park_if_dirty` and the tick retries the fast-forward once the files are clean, without new gates when main has not moved.
3. Uncommitted files the branch does not touch stay harmless, as today.

acceptance.text: An item whose branch changes a tracked file that is uncommitted in the repository root does not start gating: it is blocked with a message naming the files and the fix, and shows as NEEDS YOU; no gate run or review is started
A Dirty error at fast-forward time parks an approved item instead of failing it; once the files are clean the tick merges it without new gates when main has not moved
Uncommitted files the branch does not touch do not block anything (existing tests unchanged)
cli_merge.rs covers: overlap before gates, dirty at fast-forward after approval, unrelated dirty file
cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test --workspace pass

title: Merge: a failed reviewer start keeps the item in review instead of repeating the gates; ensure_submitted presses at least once
body:
Observed 2026-11-13 20:23 (asf-134, review round 1): the reviewer asf-164 did not start: `timeout: kick-off prompt not submitted: agent still idle after 0 submit key press(es) (failed start 1 of 2; the next tick starts a fresh reviewer)`. The machine was busy with three `cargo test` runs. Two things went wrong:

1. The item went `reviewing -> queued -> rebasing -> gating`: a failed reviewer start cost a complete second gate run (10 minutes) although neither the branch nor main had changed.
2. `0 submit key press(es)` after the whole start timeout means `ensure_submitted` (asf-109) never pressed Enter, so the retry that exists for exactly this case did nothing.

Wanted:
1. After a failed reviewer start the item stays in `reviewing` and the next tick starts a fresh reviewer; gates are repeated only when the branch head or the default branch moved since they passed (the same rule an approved item already follows).
2. Find why `ensure_submitted` pressed nothing in this case (prompt typed but the pane not yet interactive? the wait consumed the whole budget before the first press?) and make it press at least once before the timeout; the message keeps the count.
3. A test for each: a start failure followed by a successful start runs the gates once; a pane that stays idle with the prompt in its input gets a submit key before the timeout.

acceptance.text: After a failed reviewer start the next tick starts a fresh reviewer without a new gate run, unless the branch head or the default branch moved since the gates passed

Owner 2026-11-13 ('the reviewer again did not start because it did not get Enter'): ensure_submitted does not wait the whole worker.start_timeout_ms before its first key press. It waits a short first window (about 15 s, a constant or a config key), then presses Enter if the agent is idle and the kick-off line is in the input box, and repeats with the remaining budget; today a prompt that Herdr typed but did not submit sits unsent for 3 minutes (seen on asf-155, asf-157, asf-164, asf-173)

A pane that is still idle with the kick-off prompt unsent gets at least one submit key press before the start timeout; the failure message keeps the press count and says which check withheld the key (state not idle / kick-off line not found on the pane)
Tests cover: start failure then success runs the gates once; idle pane with unsent prompt receives a submit key within the short first window; a pane where the line is not found reports that reason

title: Rename: the product, binary, crates and env vars become Klobuk; LICENSE and README for the first public release
body:
The project is published as **Klobuk — the autonomous software factory** (repository `numikel/klobuk`, licence Apache-2.0). Today everything is still called `asf` / auto-software-factory. Rename it in one pass, as the last task of the round, when no other branch is open.

Decisions already taken by the owner (do not re-open; ask through AskUserQuestion only for something not covered here):
- Binary: `klobuk` (was `asf`). Crates: `klobuk` (binary), `klobuk-core`, `klobuk-store`, `klobuk-runtime`, `klobuk-vcs`, `klobuk-method` (directories under `crates/` renamed to match). Rust paths `asf_core::` etc. become `klobuk_core::`.
- The data directory stays `.factory/` (no migration). File names inside it stay.
- Environment variables: `ASF_ISSUE`, `ASF_RUN` and every other `ASF_*` become `KLOBUK_*`. No fallback to the old names (no worker is running when this merges).
- Default issue prefix for a NEW repository: `kb` (was `asf`). An existing repository keeps the prefix stored in its config; this repository keeps `asf` (`.factory/config.toml` already says so and `.factory/issues.jsonl` is not rewritten).
- Everything a human reads says Klobuk / `klobuk`: clap name and about text, help, error and hint texts (`start it again: klobuk serve --dispatch`), TUI header, worker brief and `CLAUDE.local.md` text, hook commands written into worker settings (`klobuk hook …`), status line, Herdr metadata source, methodology manifests, README, CLAUDE.md, CI workflow.
- Name of the default methodology `asf-default` becomes `klobuk-default` (directory and manifest); a config that still says `asf-default` is accepted as an alias with one line of deprecation notice.
- Add `LICENSE` (Apache-2.0 full text) and `license = "Apache-2.0"` plus `repository = "https://github.com/numikel/klobuk"` in the workspace package metadata.
- README: title "Klobuk — the autonomous software factory", and a short section "Why Klobuk": a kłobuk is a household spirit from the folklore of Warmia and Masuria, usually seen as a black hen or rooster; it lives in the homestead, brings goods to it and works for the household as long as it is looked after. The factory works for the owner of the repository as long as it is fed with tasks and a budget.

Not in scope: the git history, the tags, `.factory/issues.jsonl`, the worktree directory name, design docs outside the repo.

Notes:
- Do the mechanical part with `git mv` for directories and a scripted replace, then fix what the script cannot know (word boundaries: `asf-` issue ids in tests and fixtures are data, not the product name; test repos created by tests may keep an explicit `asf` prefix where the test passes it, but tests of the DEFAULT prefix expect `kb`).
- After the rename: `git grep -nI -E "\basf\b|ASF_|auto-software-factory"` must return only intended leftovers (this repo's own issue prefix in `.factory/`, historical notes); list them in the report.
- `Cargo.lock` is regenerated by cargo, not edited by hand.

acceptance.text: cargo build produces a binary named klobuk; klobuk --help, klobuk --version and every user-facing text say Klobuk/klobuk; no command, hint or brief tells the user to run asf
Crates and directories are klobuk, klobuk-core, klobuk-store, klobuk-runtime, klobuk-vcs, klobuk-method; Rust paths use klobuk_*
Workers get KLOBUK_ISSUE and KLOBUK_RUN (and any other former ASF_* variable under the new name); lane resolution, hooks and the worker-side refusals read the new names
klobuk repo init in a fresh repository uses the prefix kb by default; a repository whose config says prefix asf keeps working unchanged (test for both)
The methodology klobuk-default ships; a config naming asf-default is accepted with a one-line deprecation notice
LICENSE holds the Apache-2.0 text; workspace metadata has license and repository; README has the new title and the Why Klobuk section
git grep for the old names returns only the intended leftovers, listed in the report

title: Merge: options to stop repeating gate runs (reuse_verification; verify_main_after editable)
body:
Measured 2026-11-13: every task waits for four full gate runs of about 10 minutes each, all on the one gate slot: the worker's own run, the verification after `finish`, the queue gates after the rebase, and (with `verify_main_after`) the gates on main. Two of them often test a tree that was already tested.

Wanted, as options the owner can switch (owner's decision: options, not hard-wired behaviour):

1. `[merge] reuse_verification` (bool, default true). When an item reaches the queue gates and (a) its run was verified, (b) the rebase was a no-op (the branch already sits on the current head of the default branch) and (c) the branch head equals the head that was verified, the queue does not run the gates again: it records the verification results as the item's gate results, says so in the event log and the Queue view (`gates reused from verification`), and goes on to the review. Any real rebase, or a new commit after verification, runs the gates as today.
2. `merge.verify_main_after` becomes an editable key (Config view, `asf config set`), with a description that says what it costs (one more full gate run per merge) and when it is redundant (after a fast-forward main is exactly the tree the queue gates passed). The key itself already exists.

Notes:
- "Verified head" must be stored with the run or the merge item when verification succeeds; do not infer it from timestamps.
- The reviewer still reviews; this is only about gate runs.
- Keep the behaviour with `reuse_verification = false` byte-for-byte as today (existing tests unchanged).

acceptance.text: With merge.reuse_verification on (default), an item whose run was verified, whose rebase was a no-op and whose head equals the verified head skips the queue gates; the event log and the Queue view say the gates were reused; the review runs as usual
A real rebase or a commit after verification runs the queue gates as today; with the option off nothing changes (existing tests untouched)
merge.verify_main_after and merge.reuse_verification are editable keys with descriptions that state their cost; key-count tests updated
cli_merge.rs covers: reuse, real rebase, new commit after verification, option off
cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test --workspace pass

title: Brief: worker.self_test option, targeted tests by default instead of the full suite
body:
Measured 2026-11-13: before `finish` every worker runs `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy` and the full `cargo test --workspace` itself (the brief's closing ritual asks for the repository gates), and then the factory runs the same gates again as verification. With two workers and the gate slot busy this is three full test runs at once on one machine: each takes longer, and on Windows the linker fails at random (LNK1104), so workers retry.

Wanted: an option for how much a worker tests on its own.

- `[worker] self_test` = `"targeted"` | `"full"`, default `"targeted"`, editable (Config view, `asf config set`).
- `targeted`: the brief tells the worker to run the fast gates (format, lint) and only the tests that cover what it changed (the test files in its scope, the package it touched), and explicitly NOT the full suite: verification runs the full gates right after `finish` and sends a failure back.
- `full`: the brief keeps today's wording (run every configured gate before `finish`).
- The wording is language-neutral: it speaks of "the gates in `.factory/config.toml`" and "the tests of what you changed", not of cargo. The list of gate commands shown in the brief comes from the config, as today.

Notes: the brief text lives in `crates/asf-core/src/brief.rs`; there are snapshot-like tests of the brief.

acceptance.text: worker.self_test = targeted (default) makes the brief ask for the fast gates and only the tests of what the worker changed, and says the full gates run in verification; full keeps today's wording
The brief wording is language-neutral and takes the gate commands from the config

The brief also says how to wait for the worker's own long command: run it in the foreground or wait for that one process, never poll for 'any cargo process' (gates and other workers run cargo too) and never through a shell that needs a permission prompt (powershell)
The key is editable (Config view and asf config set) with a description; key-count tests updated
Tests cover both values of the option in the rendered brief
cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test --workspace pass

title: TUI Queue: expand an item into its steps (each gate, review round, merge) with live timers, like a CI job page
body:
Owner's wish (2026-11-13): "One thing I miss in the Queue view: seeing the steps, the way GitHub Actions shows them."

Today a queue row shows five stage dots (rebase, gates, review, merge, main gates). It does not show what happens inside a stage: which gate runs now and for how long, which gates already passed and how long each took, which review round it is and who reviews, why an item waits (gate slot busy with another item), how many attempts it has behind it.

Wanted: the selected item in the Queue view expands into a list of steps, like a job page in GitHub Actions:

```
▾ asf-134  feat/asf-134                                   attempt 2 · 14 min
    ✓ rebase onto main (c1b3a61)                                     1 s
    ✓ gate fmt                                                       1 s
    ✓ gate clippy                                                    1 s
    ● gate test                                          running  6 min 12 s
    ○ review  round 1
    ○ merge
    ○ gates on main
```

- One line per step: every configured gate by its name from the config (not hard-coded fmt/clippy/test), the review with its round and the reviewer's run id and model once started, the merge, and the gates on main only when `verify_main_after` is on.
- Marks: done, running (with a live timer), waiting, failed, skipped (with the reason: `gate skipped: when-condition`, `review skipped: this patch was approved before`, `gates reused from verification`).
- A waiting item says what it waits for: `waiting for the gate slot (asf-163 is on gate test)`.
- Earlier attempts of the same item are folded into one line each (`attempt 1: gate test failed after 9 min`), expandable.
- `Enter` on a gate step opens that gate's output (the overlay that exists for the whole item today, scrolled to that gate); on the review step it shows the verdict text; `f` on the review step focuses the reviewer pane.
- Rows that are not selected stay one line with the stage dots, as today. `l`/`h` (or Enter on the row) expand and collapse.
- `asf tui --once --view queue` prints the first item expanded, so the view can be checked in tests and screenshots.

Notes:
- Live per-gate progress needs the name and start time of the gate in flight and the results of the gates already finished in the current run; today results arrive only when the whole run ends (`GateSlot`). Expose finished gates of the run in flight to the snapshot.
- Durations of finished steps come from `gate_results` and the event log (`merge.state`, `merge.review_started`, `merge.review_approved`, ...); do not invent timestamps.

acceptance.text: MINIMUM (owner, 2026-11-13: 'at least in the gates stage we should be able to look inside'): while a gate is running, Enter on it opens its LIVE output (the tail of the command's stdout/stderr, refreshed while the overlay is open, with the elapsed time), not only the output after the run has ended

Owner 2026-11-13 ('in the TUI I see that nothing happens with 112', it sat 28 min in finishing while two other items used the gate slot, then 21 min in verifying): a run that waits says why, in the Now and Agents views too, not only in Queue. A run in finishing shows 'waiting for the gate slot: asf-163 is on gate test, 12 min' (whose job holds the slot, which gate, for how long, and how many jobs are ahead); a run in verifying shows the gate in flight with a live timer and its finished gates; Enter on such a row opens the same live gate output

The selected queue item expands into one line per step: rebase, every configured gate by name, review with round and reviewer, merge, gates on main only when enabled; each with a mark and a duration, the running one with a live timer
Skipped steps say why; a waiting item says what it waits for (which item holds the gate slot and on which gate)
Earlier attempts of the item are folded lines that can be expanded
Enter on a finished gate step opens that gate's output; on the review step the verdict; f focuses the reviewer pane
Unselected rows keep today's one-line form; asf tui --once --view queue prints the first item expanded and tests cover it; a test covers the waiting text of a finishing run in the Now view
Gate names come from the config, nothing is hard-coded to cargo

title: Config: offer the full model set (fable, opus, sonnet, haiku) for worker, reviewer and planner
body:
Owner 2026-11-13: "Why is fable nowhere in the model choices? We should have the full set: haiku, sonnet, opus and fable."

`crates/asf-core/src/config_edit.rs` has `const MODELS: &[&str] = &["opus", "sonnet", "haiku"];`. The Config view and `asf config set` offer only these for `worker.model`, `review.model` and `planner.model`. Claude Code accepts the alias `fable` (`claude --help`: "an alias for the latest model (e.g. 'fable', 'opus', or 'sonnet')").

Wanted:
- The choice list is `fable`, `opus`, `sonnet`, `haiku` (strongest first) for every model key, in the Config view (h / l cycle) and in the validation of `asf config set`.
- The config template comments and anything else that lists models (doctor, help texts) know `fable`.
- A full model id (`claude-…`) stays accepted through Enter as today. Defaults do not change.

## Cost: no price table to maintain (operator's check, 2026-11-13)

An earlier version of this issue asked for a price row for fable and a live price refresh. That was based on a wrong assumption and is withdrawn: the factory has **no price table**. `asf hook status` (`crates/asf/src/commands/hook.rs`, `fn status`) stores `cost.total_cost_usd` exactly as the Claude Code status line reports it. Claude Code prices the session itself, per real model id, including cache writes and cache reads, so a new model needs no change here and there is nothing to refresh.

What is still worth doing in this issue, small:
- Say where the number comes from, once, where the owner looks: the description of the budget keys in the Config view and the footer of `asf cost` ("cost as reported by Claude Code for each session: API list prices including cache reads and writes; on a subscription plan this is an equivalent, not a bill").
- Do not add a pricing section, a price list or any network call.

For the record, the research result (kept so nobody repeats it): Anthropic has no machine-readable price endpoint (the Models API returns no prices); the public LiteLLM list `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/main/model_prices_and_context_window.json` carries per-token prices for every current Claude model and matched Anthropic's published table on 2026-11-13 (fable 5.2: 8 / 40, opus 5.5: 4 / 20, sonnet 5.5: 2 / 10, haiku 5.5: 0.10 / 0.50 USD per MTok). It would be the source if the factory ever priced runs itself (for example for an agent that reports no cost).

acceptance.text: worker.model, review.model and planner.model offer fable, opus, sonnet, haiku (in this order) in the Config view and accept each of them in asf config set; full model ids are still accepted; defaults unchanged
Template comments, doctor and help texts that list models include fable

The budget key descriptions and the asf cost output say in one line where the cost comes from (Claude Code's own session cost, API list prices including cache, an equivalent on a subscription plan); no price table, pricing section or network call is added

The tests no longer pin the number of editable keys as a literal: they compare the key lists with each other (EDITABLE, APPLIES, FIELDS, Config view), so a task that adds a config key does not have to touch a count in unrelated test files
Tests cover the new choice in the list and in set_key validation

title: Linux: parallel exports use their own temp file, pwsh shell picks the right program, CI and README name the python test prerequisite
body:
The CI workflow runs on `windows-latest` and `ubuntu-latest`, but the project was only ever built and tested on Windows. Before the first public release the operator ran the three gates in a Linux container (`rust:1`, clean clone of `main` at 0b7d3b4, `python` installed): `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass, `cargo test --workspace` ends with 1362 passed and 2 failed. Fix both failures and the hidden test prerequisite. You work on Windows and cannot run Linux here: the operator reruns the container after your change, so reason from the evidence below and keep the fixes platform-neutral rather than `cfg`-ing the tests away.

## Finding 1: parallel auto-exports race on one shared temp file (real bug, Linux)

`crates/klobuk/tests/cli_export.rs` `parallel_comments_no_lock_errors` fails on Linux: three of the parallel `issue comment` processes exit 1 with

```
{"error":{"code":"io","message":"<repo>/.factory/issues.jsonl: No such file or directory (os error 2); retry: No such file or directory (os error 2)"},"ok":false}
```

Cause: `write_export` (`crates/klobuk/src/commands/export.rs`) writes every export to the same `issues.jsonl.tmp` and renames it. Two processes that export at the same time share that name: one removes or renames the other's temp file, and the loser's `rename` fails with ENOENT, so a command that had already committed its change to the store reports an error. On Windows the timing hides it.

Wanted:
- Each export writes to a temp file of its own (for example a name with the process id and a counter or random suffix, in the same directory so the rename stays atomic), so parallel exports never touch each other's temp file. The last finished rename wins; every exporter wrote a complete snapshot, so any winner is a valid file.
- The symlink refusals stay (destination and temp file), and a stale temp file left by a crashed run is still cleaned up or harmless: say in the report how old leftovers are handled.
- The Windows fallback (the target is held open by another process) keeps working, but must not delete the destination and then fail, leaving no export at all: if the second rename fails, the previous export must still be there or the error must say plainly that it is gone.
- A failed auto-export after a successful store write must not look like a failed command to a parallel writer in the normal case. Keep the existing behaviour for a real IO error (disk full, permission): it is reported.

## Finding 2: `shell = "pwsh"` cannot work outside Windows

`crates/klobuk-vcs/tests/gates.rs` `shell_pwsh_runs_through_powershell` fails with "cannot start `Write-Output hello-from-pwsh`: No such file or directory". `build` in `crates/klobuk-vcs/src/gates.rs` always starts a program named `powershell`. That name exists only on Windows (Windows PowerShell); PowerShell 7 on Linux and macOS is `pwsh`.

Wanted:
- `shell = "pwsh"` and `shell = "powershell"` start `powershell` on Windows (unchanged) and `pwsh` elsewhere.
- When the shell program is missing, the gate result says which program was not found and that the gate asked for it through `shell = "…"` (today the message names only the gate command, which misleads).
- The test must not fail on a machine without PowerShell: it checks the program choice per platform without needing the program (a unit test of the command that `build` produces), and the end-to-end run through PowerShell stays as a test that runs where the program exists and says "skipping: …" on stderr where it does not, like `export_refuses_symlink_destination` does for symlinks.

## Finding 3: the tests need `python` and nothing says so

The test suites fake gates with `python -c …` and `python <script>` (`crates/klobuk-vcs/tests/gates.rs`, `crates/klobuk/tests/cli_merge.rs`, `cli_run.rs`, `cli_serve.rs`, `cli_github.rs`, `crates/klobuk/src/worker.rs` tests). In a container without a `python` command 97 tests failed with "cannot start `python …`: No such file or directory". Do not rewrite those tests.

Wanted:
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` installs Python before the tests on both systems (`actions/setup-python`, a pinned major version of the action, Python 3.x) so the `python` command exists on `ubuntu-latest` as well.
- `README.md` gets a short "Development" note: the three gate commands, and that the tests need `python` (3.x) on `PATH`; PowerShell is optional. Keep the README's existing structure and tone.

## Out of scope

Do not change what the gates do on Windows, the JSONL format, or any test that passes on both systems today. Do not add a dependency for the temp file name.

acceptance.text: Parallel exports never share a temp file: every write_export uses a temp file name of its own in the destination directory, and parallel_comments_no_lock_errors passes without a cfg attribute or a retry loop in the test
A test pins that two exports running at the same time both succeed and leave one complete, parseable issues.jsonl and no temp file behind
The symlink refusals for the destination and the temp file still hold, and the Windows fallback never ends with neither the old nor the new export on disk without saying so in the error
shell = pwsh and shell = powershell start powershell on Windows and pwsh on other systems; a unit test pins the program name per platform without running it
A gate whose shell program is missing reports the missing program and the shell setting that asked for it
shell_pwsh_runs_through_powershell runs where the program exists and prints a skipping line where it does not; it never fails only because PowerShell is absent
ci.yml installs Python with actions/setup-python on both systems before the test step
README.md has a Development note with the three gate commands and the python prerequisite of the tests

README.md has a short Platforms note that states the facts as of this release and nothing more: Windows is the system the factory is developed and used on daily; on Linux the test suite passes but no live factory run (Herdr plus Claude Code workers) has been done yet; macOS is untested; reports from Linux and macOS users are welcome

title: Make the remote round-trip test independent of the machine's git identity; let both CI systems finish
body:
The first CI run on GitHub (run 45187242402, commit ee9a701) failed on `ubuntu-latest`. `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy` passed on both systems. `cargo test --workspace` on Linux passed every test binary of `klobuk`, `klobuk-core`, `klobuk-runtime`, `klobuk-store` and the `gates` and `git` suites of `klobuk-vcs`, then failed one test. The Windows job was cancelled by the matrix as soon as Linux failed, so its test result is unknown.

## Finding 1: one test needs the machine's git identity

`crates/klobuk-vcs/tests/github.rs`, `push_and_pull_ff_round_trip_through_the_remote`:

```
panicked at crates/klobuk-vcs/tests/github.rs:13:5:
git ["commit", "-q", "--amend", "-m", "feat x (amended)", "--no-edit"]: Committer identity unknown
*** Please tell me who you are.
fatal: empty ident name (for <runner@...>) not allowed
```

Cause: `commit_file` in that file passes `-c user.name=t -c user.email=t@x`, but the `git commit --amend` a few lines below (lines 62-65) passes no identity and the test repository has none configured. The GitHub runner has no global git identity and its user has an empty full name, so git refuses. A developer machine has a global identity, and a container running as root derives a name from the account, which is why the local gates and the Linux container run on 2026-11-23 were green.

Wanted:

title: Make the default-export path test independent of the 8.3 spelling of the temp directory
body:
The second CI run on GitHub (run 45192359259, commit 6d177c1) is green on `ubuntu-latest` and red on `windows-latest`. `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy` pass on both. On Windows `cargo test --workspace` fails one test and stops at that test binary:

```
---- export_default_path_and_determinism stdout ----
panicked at crates\klobuk\tests\cli_export.rs:27:5:
assertion `left == right` failed
  left: "C:/Users/runneradmin/AppData/Local/Temp/klobuk-test-MgFddI/.factory/issues.jsonl"
 right: "C:/Users/RUNNER~1/AppData/Local/Temp/klobuk-test-MgFddI/.factory/issues.jsonl"
```

Cause: on the Windows runner the `TEMP` variable holds the 8.3 short form of the temp directory (`RUNNER~1`). The test builds the expected path from the temp directory as given (short form), while `klobuk export` reports the path under the repository root as git resolves it (long form). Both name the same file; the test compares the two strings. The program is right, the test is too strict about spelling.

The operator reproduced this on the development machine: with `TEMP` and `TMP` set to the 8.3 short form of a long-named directory on the system drive (the drive that holds the tests' usual temp directory has no short names, which is why it never showed), `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` gives 43 suites green (1369 tests) and exactly this one failure. So no other test is known to depend on the spelling of the temp path.

Wanted:
- `export_default_path_and_determinism` passes whether the temp directory is given in its short or its long form. It must still prove that the default export goes to `.factory/issues.jsonl` of the repository the command ran in, not merely that some path is printed: compare what the two paths resolve to (the standard library can do that), not their spelling. No new dependency.
- Look for other places in the workspace tests that compare a path printed by the binary with a path built from the temp directory by string equality. Evidence says there are none that fail, so do not rewrite passing tests; list in the report what you looked at (file and line) and why each is safe or was fixed. If a shared helper in `crates/klobuk/tests/common/mod.rs` makes the next such test safe by default, prefer that over a local patch, and say which you chose.
- Do not change what `klobuk export` prints.

Checking it: if you can run one `cargo test -p klobuk --test cli_export` with `TEMP` and `TMP` pointing at an 8.3 short path without a permission prompt, do it and report the result before and after. If that needs a tool you are not allowed to use, do not work around it: say so in the report. The operator reruns the whole suite under the short temp path after your change either way.

## Out of scope

No change to product code, to CI, or to tests that pass under the short temp path.

title: Make the five workspace crates packageable for crates.io
body:
Klobuk 0.1.0 is public on GitHub. The next step is publishing the five workspace crates to crates.io (`klobuk-core`, `klobuk-store`, `klobuk-vcs`, `klobuk-runtime`, `klobuk`) so the name is reserved and `cargo install klobuk` works. A trial packaging run on 2026-11-23 showed the workspace cannot be packaged yet. Make it packageable. You do not publish anything: the owner runs the real `cargo publish` with their own token. Never run `cargo publish` without `--dry-run`, never run `cargo login`, never ask for or read a token.

Read the current Cargo documentation first (Context7 or https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/publishing.html and https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/manifest.html): do not rely on memory for manifest fields or `cargo package` behaviour.

## Finding 1: internal dependencies have no version

`[workspace.dependencies]` in the root `Cargo.toml` declares the four internal crates with `path` only. Cargo refuses to package a crate whose dependency has no version requirement ("all dependencies must have a version requirement specified when packaging").

Wanted: each internal dependency carries `version = "0.1.0"` next to `path`, and the version stays in one place per crate so the next release is a small edit. Say in the report where a release bump must touch.

## Finding 2: files read from outside the crate directory

A packaged crate contains only its own directory, so these builds or tests break for anyone who gets the crate from crates.io:

- `crates/klobuk/src/commands/method.rs` embeds the shipped methodologies with `include_str!("../../../../methodologies/...")` (seven files under `methodologies/` at the repository root). `crates/klobuk/tests/cli_method.rs` and `crates/klobuk/tests/cli_plan.rs` reach the same directory through `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` + `../../methodologies`.
- `crates/klobuk-core/src/run.rs` (test module, line 155) reads `../../klobuk-store/src/schema.sql` to check that `RunState::ALL` and `MergeState::ALL` match the `CHECK (... IN (...))` lists of the schema.

Wanted:
- The shipped methodologies live inside the `klobuk` crate directory, as one copy (move with `git mv`, no duplicate at the root). Update every path that points at them: the `include_str!` calls, the two test files, the `.gitignore` exception `!methodologies/**/*.md`, and any mention in `README.md` or `CLAUDE.md`.
- The schema consistency check keeps running in the workspace but no longer makes `klobuk-core` read a sibling crate's file. `klobuk-store` owns `schema.sql` and already depends on `klobuk-core`, so the check belongs there. `klobuk-core` stays free of IO and of a dependency on `klobuk-store`. The check must still fail when a state is added on one side only: prove it once by breaking it and say so in the report.

## Finding 3: package metadata

The crates have `description`, `license` and `repository` only. Add what the Cargo docs recommend for a published crate: `readme`, `homepage`, `keywords` (at most five), `categories` (valid crates.io category slugs: check the list, do not guess), and `documentation` only if it points somewhere real. Each of the five crates gets a description that says what that crate is. The `klobuk` crate page on crates.io must show the project README. Library crates may share it or carry a two-line README of their own that points at the main one: pick one and say which.

Every packaged crate must contain the Apache-2.0 licence text (`LICENSE`), not only the SPDX field.

## Checks to run and report

- `cargo publish --dry-run --workspace` finishes without an error. If the installed Cargo does not support `--workspace` for `publish`, report the Cargo version and run the dry run per crate in dependency order instead, explaining any step that cannot pass before the earlier crate exists on crates.io.
- `cargo package --list -p <crate>` for each of the five crates: paste the lists in the report. They must contain the sources, `Cargo.toml`, the licence and the README, and must not contain `.factory/`, `docs/`, `.worktrees/`, test databases or anything outside the crate's purpose. No package may exceed 10 MB.
- The three gates stay green.

## Out of scope

No behaviour change in the binary, no change to the methodology contents, no version bump, no CI publishing workflow, no change to the install section of `README.md` beyond paths that moved (the `cargo install klobuk` line is added after the real publication).

body: Spec conflict: 'zero commits ahead must be refused' vs 'keep the ancestor path unchanged'. A branch with 0 commits ahead of HEAD is always an ancestor of HEAD, so the existing path accepts it, and worker.rs:283 (rollback of a freshly created lane) relies on that. Refusing it would leak worktrees on rollback. My plan: apply the count>0 guard ONLY to the new git-cherry path (it is unreachable for 0-ahead anyway), keep the ancestor path as is, and test the guard via a private helper unit test in git.rs. Zero-ahead lanes stay removable through worktree_remove; asf-6 (lane clean) must exclude fresh lanes itself. Tell me if you want different semantics.

(2) States accepted after the timeout: idle, done AND working (a working agent is up; closing its workspace would destroy live work). blocked and unknown now lead to the retry (before, blocked counted as 'up' and the kick prompt was typed into the blocked pane). (4) The retry reopens the pane via a new open_pane helper, so it gets a fresh Claude --session-id (reusing the UUID could fail with 'session already in use' if the first claude got that far) and the run row is updated to the new workspace/pane. (5) run.start_retry event: actor orchestrator, payload {reason: '<timeout message>; agent state after re-read: <state>', workspace_id: <abandoned workspace>}. When a key press sets the same text again before the next advance() (press `t` twice while a tick runs -> "busy: tick"; `s` twice on a non-ready issue; the same "sent ..." status twice), advance() finds the old stamp and the new message vanishes as soon as the FIRST one's 4 s are up, not 4 s after the second press. Either guard those arms in handle_key with the table's views, or widen the table's `views` and add the missing keys, so that help and footer describe what the keys do.

author: agent:asf-32
body:
Choices the brief left open or where the mockup and the rules text differ (asf-32):
1. Merge rows take `r retry` (asf merge retry), not `v verify` as the mockup shows on its "merge failed" row: the rules map `v` to `asf run verify` (runs) and `r` to `asf merge retry` (merge items). `a` on a failed/stalled/over_budget run or a merge row only sets a status naming the right key.
2. A QUESTION comment has no pane to read, so `a` on a question row opens a one-line input and posts an ANSWER comment from lane human with --reply-to (what `asf issue finish` checks), instead of the pane overlay. A blocked-run row still opens the asf-30 overlay. New Action::Answer, tui::post_answer.
3. A blocked, stalled or over_budget run is listed once, in NEEDS YOU, and not again in RUNNING (selection walks NEEDS YOU then RUNNING, so a duplicate would be ambiguous). `runs` is active-only, so failed runs come from a new Snapshot.failed_runs (newest run of each live issue, when it failed and nothing is active).
4. The Now view hides the one-line banner (the section lists the waiters); the other views keep it. The header "N waiting" now counts NEEDS YOU rows of all sources, so header and section agree.
5. Row age = time since the run entered its current state (newest run.state event, else finished_at/started_at); questions use created_at, merge items updated_at.
6. DONE TODAY uses the local UTC offset from the time crate. `time/local-offset` is enabled workspace-wide only transitively (ratatui-widgets); Cargo.toml is outside my scope. If the offset cannot be read (multithreaded Linux) it falls back to UTC. Declaring the feature in crates/asf/Cargo.toml would make it explicit.
7. The Now footer is the mockup line (j / k move, a answer, f focus pane, Enter open issue, Tab next view, ? help, q quit) built from the binding table; `v verify` and `r retry` are printed on their rows and listed in the help view, not in the footer.
8. NO_COLOR: App.color is read from the environment only in run_once/run_interactive; the renderer strips fg/bg from the finished buffer, so bold, dim and reverse stay and no widget needs its own switch.
9. Small choices: reviewer rows show cost / budget like worker rows (the rules text says so; the mockup omits it); review issues and epics are not counted in UP NEXT, review issues not in DONE TODAY; UP NEXT / DONE TODAY with nothing to show print a dim sentence; label column is 15 wide so `merge blocked` keeps a gap.
10. Process note: the Now model/render code was written before its tests in this run; the tests were then added and the mutation break-checks run (see the report).

Choices the brief left open, settled in the Agents rebuild:
1. State label of a reviewer whose run has gone wrong (stalled, over_budget, failed) is the run state, not "reviewing": the red square would otherwise sit next to a calm word. Blocked is still "asking"; every other reviewer run is "reviewing".
2. Session name in the preview title: the store does not record it (LastRun.session_name is None), so the view uses it when set and otherwise derives it with the same rule as worker::session_name (copied into agents.rs, pinned by a test with the worker's own examples). Reviewers get the review-<id> prefix.
3. A reviewer row whose round is unknown shows "<title> · <model>" without " · rN". The model is [review] model (snapshot.review_model).
4. The old "m merge" key stays on the Agents view as a help-only binding (not in the footer); the footer carries the five keys of the mockup.
5. Narrow screens: column widths follow the content; below the sum the last-activity column gives up width before the task does; the preview is drawn only when the area has at least 9 rows (3 for the table, 6 for the panel).
6. Preview refresh: App::peek_wanted() (app.rs, next to detail_wanted) plus one call in the event loop (mod.rs). It reads the selected run's pane when the view opens, when the selection moved to a pane not yet read, and after every store refresh; it is silent while the runtime is down so the loop cannot retry on every pass. The text of the previous read stays on screen while the new one loads.
7. Pane text is shown with control characters turned into blanks, so an escape sequence in a pane cannot paint on the operator's terminal.
8. Test-only edits in tests/frame.rs and tests/now_view.rs (scope granted in #266/#267): both assumed the old bordered Agents table.

body: Reopen the same run, do not start a new attempt. The worker's pane carries ASF_RUN=<first run id> in its environment and cannot change it; the hooks (scope, budget, cost from the statusline) resolve the run by that id. A new run would leave them on the finished run and the budget of round 2 would never trip. Worker::send_back prompts the agent, then sets the succeeded run back to working (exit_reason = 'sent back to the worker: review round N asked for changes'). finished_at keeps the old value because RunPatch cannot clear it (asf-core/store are out of scope); the next terminal state overwrites it and nothing reads it for a non-terminal run.

body: Reachable = the run has a pane, 'agent get' answers and the agent is not blocked or unknown (a prompt to a blocked agent would answer its dialog). A run that is still active keeps the old path (reply + BLOCKER).
