author: agent:asf-66
body:
Design (asf-66), chosen before coding:
1. A gate run leaves the tick as a THREAD owned by `serve` (GateSlot in worker.rs). The thread runs only the gate subprocesses (one run_gates call per gate, so the current gate name is known) and sends Vec<GateResult> over a channel. It touches no store and no Ctx: every store write stays on the tick thread as a short IMMEDIATE transaction; none is held across a gate run.
2. The heavy sites are split into prepare (cheap checks, rebase, state -> verifying/gating) / gates / conclude(results) (store writes, review entry, integrate, merge): Worker::verify, merge::process, merge::verify_main. Inline callers (run verify, run watch, merge tick, serve --once) run the three parts back to back, so their behaviour is unchanged.
3. One slot = at most ONE gate run in flight across all three kinds. When it frees up the order is: pending main check (verify_main_after) > head of the merge queue (lowest row id among `queued`, so FIFO; a requeue after main moved keeps its row, i.e. its place) > verification of a finished run. Nothing overtakes an item that is gating.
4. verify_main_after in the background: finalize_merged appends event merge.main_check_pending; the check ends with merge.main_checked (green) or the existing merge.main_red. Pending = pending event without a later end event, so the check also survives a restart.
5. Restart: when the serve loop starts it resets merge items left in `rebasing`/`gating` to `queued` (same row id, event merge.recovered). A run left in `verifying` is picked up by watch again (its issue is still in-review). Pending main checks are re-read from events. Nothing lives only in memory except the running thread itself.
6. Loop tick order: reap a finished gate run -> watch (blocked/stalled/questions) -> review verdicts and PR polls -> promote + close epics -> dispatch -> start the next gate run -> notify. Dispatch never waits for the queue; every tick ends in seconds.
7. Report (--json): gate_run {kind, issue, gate, seconds} or null; a tick that starts or finishes a gate run is printed, a quiet tick during a run is not.
8. --once: `serve --once`, `merge tick [--once]`, `run watch`, `run verify` BLOCK until the gates they started are finished (inline mode, no thread). Only the `serve` loop is asynchronous.
9. Left as is: Worker::send_back (one agent get + one bounded agent prompt) stays synchronous in the tick; it is bounded by worker.prompt_timeout_ms and is not a gate run.

author: agent:asf-66
body:
Additions to the design in #370 that came up while building it (nothing in #370 changed):
1. serve --until-done does not report all_done while a gate run is in flight or a check of main is owed, even when no issue is open any more: stopping would kill the run. (Assessment.gate_busy; `max_ticks` still ends the loop and the next start recovers.)
2. A gate result is dropped when its subject is gone: a merge item that is no longer 'gating' (merge skip/retry while the gates ran) or a run that is no longer 'verifying' (run abort). Otherwise a skipped item would still be merged.
3. A gate thread that dies without reporting counts as a failed gate, never a green one. An error while concluding a merge gate run fails the item (it cannot stay gating); a failed main-check or verification conclusion leaves its marker (pending event / run in verifying) so the next tick or start runs it again.
4. Recovery runs only when the serve LOOP starts, not for --once and not for merge tick: a one-shot command running next to a serve must not be mistaken for a dead one. A 'rebasing' orphan also gets a best-effort 'git rebase --abort' in its worktree.
5. One pending check of main answers for all merged items whose checks are pending (the newest is the subject, the others are 'covered' and get merge.main_checked with covered_by).
6. Priority when the slot frees up is main check > head of the merge queue > verification of a finished run, as in #370; verification last means finished-but-unverified runs hold their worker slots a little longer while a queue drains. Easy to flip in serve.rs tick_background if the operator prefers the other order.

body: Choices the brief left open. (1) An immediate notification is stored as the same attention.reminded event as a reminder (payload adds keys[] of the announced waits and immediate=true), so the reminder countdown restarts from it: the first reminder comes every_minutes after the notification (not after_minutes); with every_minutes=0 the notification counts as the once. (2) Dedupe is by wait key, not by time: question:<comment id>, blocker:<comment id>, run:<id>:<state>@<entered>, merge:<id>:<state>@<entered>, issue:blocked@<entered>; read back from the event log on every start, so a restart neither repeats nor loses. Seconds-resolution timestamps alone would merge two comments of the same second. (3) New WaitKind blocker for a BLOCKER comment to human: announced only, never reminded (the store cannot say when a blocker stops blocking). It counts while unresolved, with no later comment from the human on the issue, and younger than 24 h, so the first serve after an upgrade does not toast old blockers. (4) One alert per issue per tick, led by the most telling new wait (question > blocker > run blocked/failed/stalled/over_budget > merge failed/blocked > issue blocked); all new waits of that issue are marked announced by it. Titles: asks / is blocked / merge failed / merge blocked / is stalled / is over budget / run failed; body = first line of the text, or a stock phrase when empty. ASF_REMIND_TEXT of an alert is 'title: body'; ASF_REMIND_KIND is the wait kind (question, blocker, run_blocked, merge_failed, ...); age 0. Sound: request (the one asf-68 reminders use). (5) Tick report gets an alerts array next to reminders, and the human report prints 'notified: ...'. (6) Waits that already exist when this ships and were never announced are announced once at the first serve tick.

body: Choices made on asf-167 (all reversible): (1) First wait of ensure_submitted is a constant KICKOFF_FIRST_WINDOW_MS = 15 s (capped by start_timeout_ms), not a config key. After the key the wait is what is left of the budget, at least one first window (so 90 s gives waits 15 s + 75 s; a budget under 15 s keeps the old two equal waits). KICKOFF_ENTERS stays 1: 'repeats with the remaining budget' is read as one more wait, not a second press. A check that withholds the key before any press (state not idle, line not found) only extends the wait to the end of the budget and looks again, so a pane that turns interactive late still gets its key. (2) Root cause of asf-164 'after 0 key presses' is not proven: its message said the agent was idle, so state was fine and kickoff_in_input_box returned false (blank-free pane without the 40-char probe). Most plausible: the input box wrapped the line (box borders / breaks inside the text). The probe now ignores whitespace and box-drawing characters on both sides, and the failure message names the check that withheld the key ('no key: state not idle' / 'no key: kick-off line not found on the pane'), so the next occurrence carries evidence. (3) A failed reviewer start leaves the item in reviewing (last_error keeps the cause); the retry lives in poll_review (tick_all and serve poll both reach it) and is driven by the event log: last merge.review_started / merge.review_start_failed is the failure. It waits for a free reviewer slot like a queued item does. Before starting it compares the worktree head with merge item head_sha and the default branch with rebased_onto; if either moved the item goes to queued with merge.requeued reason branch_moved / main_moved (requeue_main_moved became requeue(reason)). Revert: git revert of the asf-167 commit.

- crates/klobuk/src/commands/export.rs (Wanted: a stale temp file from a crashed run is cleaned up or harmless): a young leftover is not harmless when the pid is reused. A short-lived CLI process almost always exports with counter 0, so a run killed between create_new and rename (worker killed by kill_tree or timeout, Ctrl-C) leaves issues.jsonl.<pid>.0.tmp. Windows recycles pids quickly, and in a container klobuk often gets the same pid every time. Any later process with that pid in the next hour fails create_new with AlreadyExists after the store commit, so the command exits 1, and the io error carries no path. Fix: when create_new returns AlreadyExists, take the next name from sibling_of (bounded retry, symlink refusal unchanged). No live process can own a file with this process's pid and a counter it has not handed out yet, so the existing file is always a leftover. Add a unit test that plants the next numbered name as a young file and expects the export to succeed.
